entry.title: Domain Adaptation of Large Language Models for Polymer-Composite Additive Manufacturing Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Fine-Tuning

author.name: Saiful Islam Sagor, Tania Haghighi, Minhaj Nur Alam, Erina Baynojir Joyee

entry.summary: Investigates practical strategies for adapting LLMs to additive manufacturing using RAG and fine-tuning, comparing approaches for domain-specific question answering about polymer-composite AM.

entry.title: AgenticAITA: A Proof-Of-Concept About Deliberative Multi-Agent Reasoning for Autonomous Trading Systems

author.name: Ivan Letteri

entry.summary: Introduces AGENTICAITA, a multi-agent LLM framework for autonomous trading that replaces traditional signal-then-execute with a deliberative loop of reasoning, negotiation, and action among specialized agents.

entry.title: Controlling Logical Collapse in LLMs via Algebraic Ontology Projection over F2

author.name: Hisashi Miyashita, Mgnite Inc

entry.summary: Introduces Algebraic Ontology Projection (AOP) that projects LLM hidden states into the Galois Field F2 to test whether models encode ontological relations in algebraic structures. Achieves up to 93.33% zero-shot inclusion accuracy on unseen concept pairs without model tuning. An interesting interpretability approach but from a small group with somewhat niche formalism.

entry.title: Constitutional Governance in Metric Spaces

author.name: Ehud Shapiro, Nimrod Talmon

entry.summary: Proposes constitutional governance in metric spaces, integrating aggregation, deliberation, amendment, and consensus into a polynomial-time protocol. Assigns metric spaces, aggregation rules, and supermajority thresholds per constitutional component.

entry.title: Coordinating Multiple Conditions for Trajectory-Controlled Human Motion Generation

author.name: Deli Cai, Haoyang Ma, Changxing Ding

entry.summary: Proposes CMC, a decoupled framework for trajectory-controlled human motion generation that coordinates text and trajectory conditions through a divide-and-conquer strategy, avoiding conflicts between conditioning signals.

entry.title: Dywave: Event-Aligned Dynamic Tokenization for Heterogeneous IoT Sensing Signal

author.name: Tomoyoshi Kimura, Denizhan Kara, Jinyang Li, Hongjue Zhao, Yigong Hu, Yizhuo Chen, Xiaomin Ouyang, Shengzhong Liu, Tarek Abdelzaher

entry.summary: Proposes Dywave, a dynamic tokenization framework for heterogeneous IoT sensing signals that uses wavelet-based hierarchical decomposition to identify meaningful temporal boundaries aligned with physical events.

entry.title: CSI-JEPA: Towards Foundation Representations for Ubiquitous Sensing with Minimal Supervision

author.name: Xuanhao Luo, Zhizhen Li, Yuchen Liu

entry.summary: Presents CSI-JEPA, a self-supervised framework for WiFi channel state information sensing that learns reusable representations from unlabeled CSI data using a JEPA-style masked prediction approach.

entry.title: Cognitive-Uncertainty Guided Knowledge Distillation for Accurate Classification of Student Misconceptions

author.name: Qirui Liu, Hao Chen, Weijie Shi, Jiajie Xu, Jia Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage knowledge distillation framework for classifying student misconceptions in education, mining high-value samples from existing data rather than synthesizing new data. Uses cognitive uncertainty to guide distillation.

entry.title: Masked Autoencoders with Limited Data: Does It Work? A Fine-Grained Bioacoustics Case Study

author.name: Wuao Liu, Mustafa Chasmai, Subhransu Maji, Grant Van Horn

entry.summary: Systematic study of masked autoencoders for bioacoustic recognition with limited weakly-annotated data, examining MAE effectiveness in modest data settings rather than massive corpora.

entry.title: Bridging the Rural Healthcare Gap: A Cascaded Edge-Cloud Architecture for Automated Retinal Screening

author.name: Nishi Doshi, Shrey Shah

entry.summary: Proposes a two-tier edge-cloud cascade for diabetic retinopathy screening using MobileNetV3-small for local triage and RETFoundDINOv2 in the cloud for severity grading. Targets rural healthcare where bandwidth and latency are constraints.

entry.title: A Non-Monotone Preconditioned Trust-Region Method for Neural Network Training

author.name: Andrea Angino, Bindi \c{C}apriqi, Shega Likaj, Ken Trotti, Rolf Krause

entry.summary: Proposes non-monotone variant of Additively Preconditioned Trust-Region Strategy (NAPTS) for training deep neural networks via domain decomposition, reducing CPU time by 30% while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Explainable Detection of Depression Status Shifts from User Digital Traces

author.name: Loris Belcastro, Francesco Gervino, Fabrizio Marozzo, Domenico Talia, Paolo Trunfio

entry.summary: Proposes an explainable framework for detecting depression-related status shifts from user digital traces using multiple BERT models to extract sentiment, emotion, and severity signals aggregated into temporal trajectories.

entry.title: Ideology Prediction of German Political Texts

author.name: Sinclair Schneider, Florian Steuber, Joao A. G. Schneider, Gabi Dreo Rodosek

entry.summary: Proposes a transformer model to project German political text orientation on a continuous left-right spectrum (-1 to 1). Compares 13 candidate foundation models for political ideology classification. Enables more nuanced political text analysis than discrete class labels.

entry.title: HDRFace: Rethinking Face Restoration with High-Dimensional Representation

author.name: Zirui Wang, Xianhui Lin, Yi Dong, Bo Wei, Gangjian Zhang, Siteng Ma, Zebiao Zheng, Xing Liu, Hong Gu, Minjing Dong

entry.summary: HDRFace proposes a face restoration framework that injects high-dimensional semantic priors from pretrained encoders into a conditional diffusion flow, addressing severe degradation cases where low-quality inputs alone are insufficient for identity recovery.

entry.title: HiSem: Hierarchical Semantic Disentangling for Remote Sensing Image Change Captioning

author.name: Man Wang, Chenyang Liu, Wenjun Li, Feng Ni, Bing Jia, Baoqi Huang, Riting Xia, Zhenwei Shi

entry.summary: HiSem proposes hierarchical semantic disentangling for remote sensing change captioning, explicitly separating coarse-grained change existence judgment from fine-grained semantic understanding to address semantic entanglement.

entry.title: A Prototyping Framework for Distributed Control of Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Junaid Ahmed Memon, Allan Andre Do Nascimento, Kostas Margellos, Antonis Papachristodoulou

entry.summary: Presents a prototyping framework for distributed control of multi-robot systems using the SPMD paradigm on a single computer. Demonstrates on a four-quadrotor position-swapping task with progressive fidelity levels from point-mass to hardware.

entry.title: An Agentic AI Framework with Large Language Models and Chain-of-Thought for UAV-Assisted Logistics Scheduling with Mobile Edge Computing

author.name: Hanwen Zhang, Dusit Niyato, Wei Zhang, Xin Lou, Malcolm Yoke Hean Low

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic AI framework using LLMs with chain-of-thought reasoning for joint UAV logistics scheduling and mobile edge computing in cloud manufacturing environments.

entry.title: IdeaForge: A Knowledge Graph-Grounded Multi-Agent Framework for Cross-Methodology Innovation Analysis and Patent Claim Generation

author.name: Joy Bose

entry.summary: IdeaForge integrates multiple innovation methodologies (TRIZ, Design Thinking, SCAMPER) through specialist agents operating over a persistent knowledge graph for cross-methodology innovation analysis and patent claim generation.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Systems in Emergency Departments: Validation Study on a ED Digital Twin

author.name: Markus Wenzel, Tobias Strapatsas, Jessika Kress, Dorothea Sauer, Nele Gessler, Horst K. Hahn

entry.summary: Develops a hybrid Discrete Event Simulation and Agent-Based Model for emergency department optimization, validated against real-world metrics from literature. Implements established resource optimization strategies.

entry.title: Adaptive mine planning under geological uncertainty: A POMDP framework for sequential decision-making

author.name: Hamza Khalifi, Jef Caers, Yassine Taha, Mostafa Benzaazoua, Abdellatif Elghali

entry.summary: Formulates mine production scheduling as a POMDP where extraction decisions anticipate future belief updates from observations, using a hybrid SA-POMDP architecture for computational tractability.

entry.title: Prime Successor Irreducibility: Turing Machine Complexity, Kolmogorov Complexity, and Weakness-Based Formulations

author.name: Ben Goertzel, Bill Lauritzen

entry.summary: Develops formal conjectures about computational irreducibility in the prime sequence, arguing that computing the next prime from a given prime cannot generally be done faster than sequential candidate testing, using both Turing machine and Kolmogorov complexity frameworks.

entry.title: Representing Higher-Order Networks: A Survey of Graph-Based Frameworks

author.name: Takaaki Fujita, Florentin Smarandache

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of graph-based frameworks for representing higher-order networks, covering multiway, hierarchical, temporal, multilayer, recursive, and tensor-based interactions beyond pairwise graphs.

entry.title: Controllable Quantum Memory Capacity in Quantum Reservoir Networks with Tunable partial-SWAPs

author.name: Erik L. Connerty, Ethan N. Evans

entry.summary: Advances quantum reservoir computing with controllable memory capacity using tunable partial-SWAP gates in recurrent architectures with memory and readout qubits.

entry.title: PRISM: Perinuclear Ring-based Image Segmentation Method for Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Classification

author.name: Larissa Ferreira Rodrigues Moreira, Leonardo Gabriel Ferreira Rodrigues, Rodrigo Moreira, Andr\'e Ricardo Backes

entry.summary: Proposes PRISM, a perinuclear ring-based segmentation method for leukemia classification that replaces explicit cytoplasmic delineation with adaptive concentric zones around the nucleus.

entry.title: CoRe-Gen: Robust Spectrum-to-Structure Generation under Imperfect Fingerprint Conditions

author.name: Tianbo Liu, Chixiang Lu, Jing Hao, Hengyu Zhang, Lifei Wang, Haibo Jiang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Addresses the condition mismatch problem in molecular structure generation from mass spectra, where models trained on clean fingerprints must operate on noisy predicted ones. Proposes CoRe-Gen to improve robustness of the spectrum-to-structure pipeline. A domain-specific chemistry/AI application.

entry.title: Neural QAOA$^{2}$: Differentiable Joint Graph Partitioning and Parameter Initialization for Quantum Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Zubin Zheng, Jiahao Wu, Shengcai Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Neural QAOA², an end-to-end differentiable framework for jointly generating graph partitions and initial parameters for quantum approximate optimization. Integrates a differentiable quantum evaluator for objective-aligned partitioning.

entry.title: Margin-calibrated Classifier Guidance for Property-driven Synthesis Planning

author.name: Najwa Laabid, Vikas Garg

entry.summary: Proposes margin-calibrated classifier guidance for steering retrosynthesis models toward desired chemical properties during inference. Addresses the insufficiency of standard cross-entropy classifiers for overriding autoregressive distributions.

entry.title: McCast: Memory-Guided Latent Drift Correction for Long-Horizon Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Penghui Wen, Yu Luo, Lintao Wang, Mengwei He, Patrick Filippi, Thomas Francis Bishop, Zhiyong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes McCast, a memory-guided latent drift correction method for precipitation nowcasting that actively corrects autoregressive drift during rollouts rather than just improving step-wise prediction accuracy.

entry.title: STAR: Semantic-Temporal Adaptive Representation Learning for Few-Shot Action Recognition

author.name: Hongli Liu, Yu Wang, Shengjie Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes STAR for few-shot action recognition, addressing semantic-temporal misalignment between static text prompts and sparse visual cues, and multi-scale temporal dynamics modeling.

entry.title: Compact Latent Manifold Translation: A Parameter-Efficient Foundation Model for Cross-Modal and Cross-Frequency Physiological Signal Synthesis

author.name: Bo Cui, Xiaowen Song, Yaowen Zhang, Shunzhe Zhang, B. J. F. van Beijnum, Monique Tabak, Ying Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CLMT, a parameter-efficient (0.09B) framework for cross-modal and cross-frequency physiological signal synthesis using discrete latent manifold translation between ECG and PPG signals.

entry.title: Generating synthetic computed tomography for radiotherapy: SynthRAD2025 challenge report

author.name: Viktor Rogowski, Maarten L. Terpstra, Niklas Wahl, Florian Kamp, Erik van der Bijl, Arthur Jr. Galapon, Christopher Kurz, Bowen Xin, Zhengxiang Sun, Hollie Min, Gregg Belous, Jason Dowling, Yan Xia, Siyuan Mei, Fuxin Fan, Arthur Longuefosse, Javier Sequeiro Gonzalez, Miguel Diaz Benito, Alvaro Garcia Martin, Fabien Baldacci, Valentin Boussot, C\'edric H\'emon, Jean-Claude Nunes, Jean-Louis Dillenseger, Zhiyuan Zhang, Jinghua Cai, Han Bing, Tan Zuopeng, Ricardo Brioso, Daniele Loiacono, Guillaume Landry, Adrian Thummerer, Matteo Maspero

entry.title: Beyond Anthropomorphism: Exploring the Roles of Perceived Non-humanity and Structural Similarity in Deep Self-Disclosure Toward Generative AI

author.name: Satoru Shibuya

entry.summary: Studies why people engage in deep self-disclosure with generative AI, finding that perceived non-humanity (reducing evaluation apprehension) and structural similarity (perceived logical alignment) are key factors beyond anthropomorphism. A large survey of 2,400 participants shows these combined perceptions dramatically increase disclosure likelihood (OR=11.35).

entry.title: OpenAaaS: An Open Agent-as-a-Service Framework for Distributed Materials-Informatics Research

author.name: Peng Kang, Bixuan Li, Xiaoya Huang, Shuo Shi, Weiqiao Zhou, Zhen Li, Yu Liu, Lei Zheng

entry.summary: Presents OpenAaaS, an open Agent-as-a-Service framework for distributed materials science research, addressing the 'last mile' problem of composing LLM agents and materials data across institutional boundaries securely.

entry.title: Weakly-Supervised Spatiotemporal Anomaly Detection

author.name: Urvi Gianchandani, Praveen Tirupattur, Mubarak Shah

entry.summary: Explores weakly supervised spatiotemporal anomaly detection in video using only video-level labels, combining multiple instance learning ranking loss with spatial localization of anomalies.

entry.title: Unsupervised learning of acquisition variability in structural connectomes via hybrid latent space modeling

author.name: Gaurav Rudravaram, Lianrui Zuo, Karthik Ramadass, Elyssa McMaster, Jongyeon Yoon, Aravind R. Krishnan, Adam M. Saunders, Chenyu Gao, Nancy R. Newlin, Praitayini Kanakaraj, Lori L. Beason Held, Murat Bilgel, Laura A. Barquero, Micah DArchangel, Tin Q. Nguyen, Laurie B. Cutting, Derek Archer, Timothy J. Hohman, Daniel C. Moyer, Bennett A. Landman

entry.summary: Introduces an unsupervised framework for separating acquisition-related variability from biological variation in structural brain connectomes using hybrid latent-space models with discrete and continuous components.

entry.title: EMA: Efficient Model Adaptation for Learning-based Systems

entry.title: Research Summary: May 14, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
A strong day for AI safety research, with multiple papers exposing fundamental vulnerabilities, alongside major advances in learning theory and reasoning.

  • A simple unified recipe achieves gold-medal-level performance on IMO/IPhO Olympiads via reverse-perplexity curriculum SFT and two-stage RL
  • LLM-based persuasion enables frontier models to override safety guardrails of other frontier models using natural language alone—a new jailbreak class
  • Scale-Sensitive Shattering resolves a longstanding open question from Anthony & Bartlett (1999), establishing a scale-sensitive fundamental theorem of PAC learning
  • Negation Neglect reveals that finetuning on documents explicitly flagging claims as false paradoxically makes models believe those claims are true
  • Persona vectors traced across OLMo-3-7B pretraining form remarkably early and persist, with direct implications for safety and alignment

On the theory side, Neural Low-Degree Filtering provides a spectral framework for understanding hierarchical feature learning in deep networks. Formal Conjectures from Google DeepMind introduces 2,615 Lean 4 problem statements including 1,029 open research conjectures as an evolving benchmark. Mechanistic analysis shows multi-agent sycophancy originates in pretraining, not RLHF, while theoretical work on weak-to-strong generalization provides rigorous grounding for scalable oversight. History Anchors demonstrates that prior harmful steps in agent action logs can flip aligned models to 91–98% unsafe compliance.

entry.summary: Demonstrates that frontier LLMs acting as simulated users can persuade other frontier LLMs to override their safety guardrails using natural language pressure techniques like peer comparison and epistemic reframing in just 5 turns.

entry.title: Formal Conjectures: An Open and Evolving Benchmark for Verified Discovery in Mathematics

author.name: Moritz Firsching, Paul Lezeau, Salvatore Mercuri, Mikl\'os Z. Horv\'ath, Ya\"el Dillies, Calle S\"onne, Eric Wieser, Fred Zhang, Thomas Hubert, Blaise Ag\"uera y Arcas, Pushmeet Kohli

entry.summary: Presents Formal Conjectures, an evolving benchmark of 2615 mathematical problem statements formalized in Lean 4, including 1029 open research conjectures for zero-contamination evaluation and 836 solved problems for proof autoformalization.

entry.title: Tracing Persona Vectors Through LLM Pretraining

author.name: Viktor Moskvoretskii, Dominik Glandorf, Jorge Medina Moreira, Tanja K\"aser, Robert West

entry.summary: Traces persona vectors (linear directions encoding traits like 'evil' or 'sycophancy') across OLMo-3-7B pretraining, finding they form remarkably early—within 0.22% of training—and remain effective for steering throughout. Highly relevant to AI safety interpretability.

entry.title: Negation Neglect: When models fail to learn negations in training

author.name: Harry Mayne, Lev McKinney, Jan Dubi\'nski, Adam Karvonen, James Chua, Owain Evans

entry.summary: Discovers 'Negation Neglect' - finetuning LLMs on documents that explicitly flag claims as false makes models believe the claims are true. Despite every sentence referencing the claim's falsity, finetuned models treat it as fact (88.6% belief rate vs 2.5% baseline), even though they correctly identify the claim as false when the same documents appear in context.

entry.title: Deep Learning as Neural Low-Degree Filtering: A Spectral Theory of Hierarchical Feature Learning

author.name: Yatin Dandi, Matteo Vilucchio, Luca Arnaboldi, Hugo Tabanelli, Florent Krzakala

entry.summary: Introduces Neural Low-Degree Filtering (Neural LoFi), a theoretical framework where deep learning dynamics decouple layer-wise, with each layer selecting directions of maximal low-degree correlation to the label, providing a tractable surrogate for understanding hierarchical feature learning.

entry.title: Do Androids Dream of Breaking the Game? Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks with BenchJack

author.name: Hao Wang, Hanchen Li, Qiuyang Mang, Alvin Cheung, Koushik Sen, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Presents BenchJack, an automated red-teaming system that audits AI agent benchmarks for reward-hacking vulnerabilities, along with a taxonomy of eight recurring flaw patterns. Argues benchmarks must be secure by design as frontier models spontaneously discover exploits.

entry.title: History Anchors: How Prior Behavior Steers LLM Decisions Toward Unsafe Actions

author.name: Alberto G. Rodr\'iguez Salgado

entry.summary: Demonstrates that frontier LLMs acting as agents will continue harmful actions when prior steps in their action log were harmful, especially with prompts encouraging consistency. Tests 17 models across six providers showing 91-98% unsafe action selection.

entry.title: Stress-Testing the Reasoning Competence of LLMs With Proofs Under Minimal Formalism

author.name: Konstantine Arkoudas, Serafim Batzoglou

entry.summary: Introduces ProofGrid, a benchmark for evaluating LLM reasoning through machine-checkable proofs using a compact natural-deduction language (NDL). Tasks span proof writing, checking, masking, and gap-filling across calibrated difficulty levels, enabling mechanical and reproducible evaluation rather than human/LLM judgment.

entry.title: CoT-Guard: Small Models for Strong Monitoring

author.name: Nirav Diwan, Han Wang, Berkcan Kapusuzoglu, Ramin Moradi, Supriyo Chakraborty, Giri Iyengar, Sambit Sahu, Huan Zhang, Gang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes CoT-Guard, using small (4B-8B) models to monitor chain-of-thought reasoning for covert misbehavior in code generation. Uses SFT+RL post-training to make small models effective monitors, achieving performance comparable to GPT-5 and Gemini-3-Flash.

entry.title: Emergent and Subliminal Misalignment Through the Lens of Data-Mediated Transfer

author.name: Baris Askin, Muhammed Ustaomeroglu, Anupam Nayak, Gauri Joshi, Guannan Qu, Carlee Joe-Wong

entry.summary: Studies emergent misalignment as data-mediated transfer, showing that harmful fine-tuning spillover depends on structural similarity between fine-tuning and evaluation prompts, prompt ambiguity, and learning reliability rather than being uniform.

entry.title: Not Just RLHF: Why Alignment Alone Won't Fix Multi-Agent Sycophancy

author.name: Adarsh Kumarappan, Ananya Mujoo

entry.summary: Challenges the common attribution of multi-agent sycophancy to RLHF, showing that pretrained base models exhibit the same vulnerability. Using activation patching, localizes the corruption to a narrow mid-layer window, with patching restoring 96% of the performance gap. Important finding for AI safety.

entry.title: Spectral Flattening Is All Muon Needs: How Orthogonalization Controls Learning Rate and Convergence

author.name: Tien-Phat Nguyen, Truong Nguyen, Minh-Phuc Truong, Tuc Nguyen, James Bailey, Trung Le

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of why the Muon optimizer works so well, proving that its spectral flattening mechanism allows much larger stable learning rates by scaling with average rather than maximum singular values of the gradient.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Language Model with Predictable Scaling Laws and Provable Benefits of Reasoning

author.name: Jason Gaitonde, Frederic Koehler, Elchanan Mossel, Joonhyung Shin, Allan Sly

entry.summary: Introduces a family of synthetic hierarchical languages generated by broadcast processes on trees, enabling precise analysis of how context length and reasoning affect autoregressive generation. Derives explicit scaling laws and proves benefits of chain-of-thought reasoning with mathematical rigor.

entry.title: Building Interactive Real-Time Agents with Asynchronous I/O and Speculative Tool Calling

author.name: Coleman Hooper, Minwoo Kang, Suhong Moon, Nicholas Lee, Eric Wen, John Wawrzynek, Michael W. Mahoney, Yakun Sophia Shao, Amir Gholami, Kurt Keutzer

entry.summary: Proposes Asynchronous I/O and speculative tool calling to enable real-time LLM agents with complex multi-turn tool calling, reducing latency from seconds to under 1 second for interactive applications.

entry.title: Learning POMDP World Models from Observations with Language-Model Priors

author.name: Valentin Six, Frederik Panse, Mathis Fajeau, Lancelot Da Costa, Mridul Sharma, Alfonso Amayuelas, Tim Z. Xiao, David Hyland, Philipp Hennig, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf

entry.summary: Introduces Pinductor, which uses LLM priors to propose and iteratively refine POMDP world models from few observation-action trajectories, reducing costly environment interaction. The approach leverages language models' prior knowledge to bootstrap structured world models for partially-observable environments.

entry.title: The Mechanism of Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Feature Elicitation from Latent Knowledge

author.name: Ryoya Awano, Taiji Suzuki

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of weak-to-strong generalization for reward model learning with two-layer neural networks, proving that multi-step SGD can learn task-specific features from weak supervision while preserving diverse pre-trained capabilities.

entry.title: On Hallucinations in Inverse Problems: Fundamental Limits and Provable Assessment Methods

author.name: David Iagaru, Nina M. Gottschling, Anders C. Hansen, Josselin Garnier

entry.summary: Develops a theoretical framework showing that hallucinations in inverse problems are fundamental consequences of ill-posedness, not just model artifacts. Derives computable bounds on minimum hallucination magnitude and introduces assessment algorithms.

entry.title: Causal Learning with the Invariance Principle

author.name: Francesco Montagna, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Shows that only two auxiliary environments are sufficient to identify the full causal graph for arbitrary nonlinear mechanisms under acyclicity and invariance assumptions. Also proves identifiability of SCM functional mechanisms, enabling correct counterfactual inference.

entry.title: Asymmetric Flow Models

author.name: Hansheng Chen, Jan Ackermann, Minseo Kim, Gordon Wetzstein, Leonidas Guibas

entry.summary: Introduces Asymmetric Flow Modeling (AsymFlow) that restricts noise prediction to low-rank subspace while keeping data prediction full-dimensional, achieving 1.57 FID on ImageNet 256×256 and enabling finetuning pretrained latent diffusion models for pixel generation.

entry.title: The critical slowing down in diffusion models

author.name: Luca Maria Del Bono, Giulio Biroli, Patrick Charbonneau, Marylou Gabri\'e

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of critical slowing down in diffusion models using the O(n) model of statistical field theory. Shows training score models exhibits critical slowing down in parameter learning that also impacts generation quality.

entry.title: No Attack Required: Semantic Fuzzing for Specification Violations in Agent Skills

author.name: Ying Li, Hongbo Wen, Yanju Chen, Hanzhi Liu, Yuan Tian, Yu Feng

entry.summary: Identifies 'specification violations' in LLM agent skills where benign inputs cause agents to break their own declared safety rules. Proposes Sefz, a semantic fuzzing tool that discovers these violations without adversarial attacks. Highly relevant to agent safety.

entry.title: Large Language Models Lack Temporal Awareness of Medical Knowledge

author.name: Zihan Guan, Qiao Jin, Guangzhi Xiong, Fangyuan Chen, Mengxuan Hu, Qingyu Chen, Yifan Peng, Zhiyong Lu, Anil Vullikanti

entry.summary: TempoMed-Bench is the first benchmark evaluating temporal awareness of LLM medical knowledge - whether models know not just what is correct but when it was correct. Reveals that LLMs struggle with time-dependent medical knowledge.

entry.title: Achieving $\epsilon^{-2}$ Sample Complexity for Single-Loop Actor-Critic under Minimal Assumptions

author.name: Ishaq Hamza, Zaiwei Chen

entry.summary: Establishes epsilon^{-2} sample complexity for single-loop single-timescale off-policy actor-critic under minimal assumptions (just irreducible Markov chain), improving over prior work requiring nested loops or strong assumptions.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Critical Scaling of Inverse Temperature in Self-Attention

author.name: Tomohiro Hayase, Ryo Karakida

entry.summary: Provides a unified theoretical framework explaining conflicting inverse-temperature scaling laws for long-context self-attention. Shows the desirable scale depends on the gap-counting function of each attention row, unifying prior laws as different gap regimes.

entry.title: All Circuits Lead to Rome: Rethinking Functional Anisotropy in Circuit and Sheaf Discovery for LLMs

author.name: Xi Chen, Mingyu Jin, Jingcheng Niu, Yutong Yin, Jinman Zhao, Bangwei Guo, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Zhaoran Wang, Yutao Yue, Gerald Penn

entry.summary: Challenges the implicit assumption that LLM functions are localized to unique circuits, showing multiple structurally distinct circuits can support the same task. Introduces Overlap-Aware Sheaf Repulsion to discover competing mechanisms.

entry.title: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs

author.name: Dylan Zhang, Yanshan Lin, Zhengkun Wu, Yihang Sun, Bingxuan Li, Dianqi Li, Hao Peng

entry.summary: Reveals that LLM-consolidated memories (abstracted from episodic traces) degrade over continuous updating—utility first rises then falls below no-memory baseline. Shows this happens even when consolidating from consistently useful experiences.

entry.title: Correct Answers from Sound Reasoning: Verifiable Process Supervision for Language Models

author.name: Kyuyoung Kim, Kevin Wang, Yunfei Xie, Peiyang Xu, Peiyao Sheng, Chen Wei, Zhangyang Wang, Jinwoo Shin, Pramod Viswanath, Sewoong Oh

entry.summary: Proposes Verifiable Process Supervision (VPS), a post-training framework that jointly optimizes prediction accuracy and reasoning quality by extracting intermediate claims from structured reasoning and evaluating them against ground-truth signals.

entry.title: In-Situ Behavioral Evaluation for LLM Fairness, Not Standardized-Test Scores

author.name: Zeyu Tang, Sang T. Truong, Deonna Owens, Shreyas Sharma, Yibo Jacky Zhang, Brando Miranda, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Argues LLM fairness should be evaluated through in-situ conversational behavior rather than standardized Q&A benchmarks. Shows prompt construction choices dominate score variance in standard benchmarks and proposes MAC-Fairness, a multi-agent conversational evaluation framework.

entry.title: WriteSAE: Sparse Autoencoders for Recurrent State

author.name: Jack Young

entry.summary: Introduces WriteSAE, the first sparse autoencoder for decomposing and editing matrix cache writes in state-space and hybrid recurrent language models (Gated DeltaNet, Mamba-2, RWKV-7), where standard residual SAEs cannot reach.

entry.title: Language-Based Agent Control

author.name: Timothy Zhou, Loris D'Antoni, Nadia Polikarpova

entry.summary: Introduces language-based agent control (LBAC), a programming model that extends type-checking guarantees from PL security to agentic applications, requiring agents to generate well-typed programs that satisfy user-specified policies.

entry.title: Revisiting Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards from a Contrastive Perspective

author.name: Feng Zhang, Xinhong Ma, Ziqiang Dong, Xi Leng, Jianfei Zhao, Xin Sun, Yang Yang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Provides a discriminative reformulation of GRPO (a key RLVR algorithm) revealing two structural limitations: likelihood-misaligned scoring and score-insensitive credit assignment. Proposes fixes that improve reasoning performance. Directly relevant to the widely-used RLVR training paradigm.

entry.title: EMO: Frustratingly Easy Progressive Training of Extendable MoE

author.name: Linghao Jin, Chufan Shi, Huijuan Wang, Nuan Wen, Zhengzhong Liu, Eric Xing, Xuezhe Ma

entry.summary: EMO progressively grows the expert pool in Mixture-of-Experts models during training, treating MoE capacity as expandable memory. Addresses the MoE efficiency paradox where adding experts increases memory/communication costs despite constant per-token FLOPs.

entry.title: Support-Conditioned Flow Matching Is Kernel Smoothing

author.name: Daniel Matsui Smola

entry.summary: Shows that the exact velocity field in support-conditioned flow matching is a Nadaraya-Watson kernel smoother with decreasing bandwidth over flow time, connecting cross-attention conditioning to classical kernel theory and predicting three failure regimes.

entry.title: Attention Once Is All You Need: Efficient Streaming Inference with Stateful Transformers

author.name: Victor Norgren

entry.summary: Introduces a stateful transformer inference model for streaming workloads where a persistent KV cache is incrementally updated as data arrives, making query latency O(|q|) independent of context size. Flash Queries pre-evaluate registered questions during idle GPU time.

entry.title: Backdoor Channels Hidden in Latent Space: Cryptographic Undetectability in Modern Neural Networks

author.name: Marte Eggen, Eirik Reiestad, Kristian Gj{\o}steen, Inga Str\"umke

entry.summary: Constructs cryptographically undetectable backdoors for modern neural network architectures by identifying backdoor channels as learned latent directions, extending prior theoretical results from stylized to practical architectures.

entry.title: Min-Max Optimization Requires Exponentially Many Queries

author.name: Martino Bernasconi, Matteo Castiglioni, Andrea Celli, Alexandros Hollender

entry.summary: Proves that finding approximate stationary points of nonconvex-nonconcave min-max optimization requires exponentially many queries (in 1/ε or d), establishing fundamental computational hardness.

entry.title: Offline Two-Player Zero-Sum Markov Games with KL Regularization

author.name: Claire Chen, Yuheng Zhang, Xinyu Liu, Zixuan Xie, Shuze Daniel Liu, Nan Jiang

entry.summary: Shows that KL regularization alone suffices for learning Nash equilibria in offline two-player zero-sum Markov games, achieving O(1/n) convergence rate under unilateral concentrability without explicit pessimism. Proposes both theoretical framework (ROSE) and practical algorithm (SOS-MD).

entry.title: Effective Context in Transformers: An Analysis of Fragmentation and Tokenization

author.name: Amirmehdi Jafari Fesharaki, Mohammadamin Rami, Aslan Tchamkerten

entry.summary: Studies how tokenization representation choice affects what finite-context transformers can learn, introducing 'fragmentation' as a concept where moving to smaller units can hurt prediction even with longer context, and 'token-level information imbalance' where some tokens carry disproportionate information.

entry.title: Do Heavy Tails Help Diffusion? On the Subtle Trade-off Between Initialization and Training

author.name: Hamza Cherkaoui, H\'el\`ene Halconruy, Antonio Ocello

entry.summary: Theoretically and empirically studies whether heavy-tailed noise helps diffusion models, showing it actually makes the statistical estimation problem harder with worse sampling-error bounds, despite intuitive appeal for heavy-tailed data.

entry.title: OSDN: Improving Delta Rule with Provable Online Preconditioning in Linear Attention

author.name: Chenyu Zhou, Hongpei Li, Yuerou Liu, Jianghao Lin, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye

entry.summary: OSDN improves the Delta Rule in linear attention with a diagonal preconditioner updated via hypergradient feedback, equivalent to per-feature key scaling, while preserving the chunkwise parallel pipeline of DeltaNet.

entry.title: When Attention Closes: How LLMs Lose the Thread in Multi-Turn Interaction

author.name: Vardhan Dongre, Joseph Hsieh, Viet Dac Lai, Seunghyun Yoon, Trung Bui, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Proposes a mechanistic explanation for why LLMs lose track of instructions in multi-turn interactions: goal-defining tokens become less accessible through attention while information persists in residuals. Introduces the Goal Accessibility Ratio (GAR) metric.

entry.title: Senses Wide Shut: A Representation-Action Gap in Omnimodal LLMs

author.name: Trung Nguyen Quang, Yiming Gao, Fanyi Pu, Kaichen Zhang, Shuo Sun, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Reveals a 'representation-action gap' in omnimodal LLMs: when text contradicts what the model sees/hears, models fail to detect the conflict despite having sensory input. Introduces IMAVB benchmark showing systematic failures across 8 open-source models and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

entry.title: 3D Primitives are a Spatial Language for VLMs

author.name: Junze Liu, Kun Qian, Florian Dubost, Kai Zhong, Arvind Srinivasan, Nan Chen, Anping Wang, Sam Zhang, Alejandro Mottini, Qingjun Cui, Tian Wang

entry.summary: Shows VLMs can generate code reconstructing 3D scenes from geometric primitives (correct object counts, positions) yet fail simpler spatial questions on the same image. Introduces SpatialBabel benchmark and uses 3D primitives as intermediate representation to boost spatial reasoning.

entry.title: From Generalist to Specialist Representation

author.name: Yujia Zheng, Fan Feng, Yuke Li, Shaoan Xie, Kevin Murphy, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Studies identifiability of task-relevant specialist representations from generalist models in a nonparametric setting, proving that temporal/task structure is identifiable without interventions, parametric assumptions, or structural constraints.

entry.title: AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation

author.name: Priyam Sahoo, Gaurav Mittal, Xiaomin Li, Shengjie Ma, Benjamin Steenhoek, Pingping Lin, Yu Hu

entry.summary: Reveals the 'Lucky Pass' problem in SWE-agent evaluation where 10.7% of passing trajectories exhibit chaotic behavior (regression cycles, blind retries). Introduces AgentLens with process-aware metrics beyond binary pass/fail.

entry.title: Scaling Laws for Mixture Pretraining Under Data Constraints

author.name: Anastasiia Sedova, Skyler Seto, Natalie Schluter, Pierre Ablin

entry.summary: Studies scaling laws for language model pretraining with data mixtures when target data (low-resource languages, specialized domains) is limited. Across 2,000+ training runs, derives scaling relationships for optimal target-data fraction as a function of model and dataset size.

entry.title: Decision Tree Learning on Product Spaces

author.name: Arshia Soltani Moakahr, Faraz Ghahremani, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi

entry.summary: Extends theoretical analysis of the top-down greedy decision tree heuristic from uniform distributions to arbitrary product distributions, showing the greedy approach constructs near-optimal trees of size quasi-polynomial in the optimal tree size.

entry.title: DP-KFC: Data-Free Preconditioning for Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning

author.name: Marc Molina Van den Bosch, Riccardo Taiello, Albert Sund Aillet, Andrea Protani, Miguel Angel Gonzalez Ballester, Luigi Serio

entry.summary: DP-KFC constructs KFAC preconditioners for DP training using synthetic noise probing rather than private or public data, addressing the geometric mismatch between anisotropic loss landscapes and isotropic DP noise.

entry.title: DiffusionHijack: Supply-Chain PRNG Backdoor Attack on Diffusion Models and Quantum Random Number Defense

author.name: Ziyang You, Liling Zheng, Xiaoke Yang, Xuxing Lu

entry.summary: Presents DiffusionHijack, a supply-chain backdoor attack on diffusion models that hijacks the PRNG to deterministically control generated images without modifying model weights. Achieves pixel-perfect reproduction and bypasses existing defenses.

entry.title: VectorSmuggle: Steganographic Exfiltration in Embedding Stores and a Cryptographic Provenance Defense

author.name: Jascha Wanger

entry.summary: Demonstrates steganographic exfiltration attacks on RAG vector databases where attackers can hide payload data in embeddings while preserving retrieval behavior, and proposes a cryptographic provenance defense.

entry.title: Good Agentic Friends Do Not Just Give Verbal Advice: They Can Update Your Weights

author.name: Wenrui Bao, Huan Wang, Jian Wang, Zhangyang Wang, Kai Wang, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: Introduces TFlow, a weight-space communication framework for multi-agent LLMs where sender agents' hidden states are compiled into transient weight perturbations for receivers, replacing token-based messaging.

entry.title: Qwen-Image-VAE-2.0 Technical Report

author.name: Zekai Zhang, Deqing Li, Kuan Cao, Yujia Wu, Chenfei Wu, Yu Wu, Liang Peng, Hao Meng, Jiahao Li, Jie Zhang, Kaiyuan Gao, Kun Yan, Lihan Jiang, Ningyuan Tang, Shengming Yin, Tianhe Wu, Xiao Xu, Xiaoyue Chen, Yan Shu, Yanran Zhang, Yilei Chen, Yixian Xu, Yuxiang Chen, Zhendong Wang, Zihao Liu, Zikai Zhou, Yiliang Gu, Yi Wang, Xiaoxiao Xu, Lin Qu

entry.summary: Qwen-Image-VAE-2.0 presents high-compression VAEs with improved reconstruction fidelity and diffusability through global skip connections, expanded channels, training on billions of images, and semantic alignment for diffusion compatibility.

entry.title: From Instance Selection to Fixed-Pool Data Recipe Search for Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Haodong Wu, Jiahao Zhang, Lijie Hu, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: AutoSelection reformulates SFT data selection from instance ranking to recipe search over a library of filtering/mixing/deduplication operators, using a two-layer solver to discover optimal data preparation pipelines under limited evaluation budgets. This is practical for improving fine-tuning efficiency.

entry.title: When is Warmstarting Effective for Scaling Language Models?

author.name: Neeratyoy Mallik, Maciej Janowski, Johannes Hog, Herilalaina Rakotoarison, Josif Grabocka, Frank Hutter, Aaron Klein

entry.summary: Studies when warmstarting (model growth from checkpoints) is effective for scaling language models, finding that preserving base model performance post-growth is unnecessary and simple growth strategies can match complex ones.

entry.title: Polyhedral Instability Governs Regret in Online Learning

author.name: Yuetai Li, Fengqing Jiang, Yichen Feng, Kaiyuan Zheng, Luyao Niu, Bhaskar Ramasubramanian, Basel Alomair, Linda Bushnell, Radha Poovendran

entry.summary: Shows that regret in online convex optimization with piecewise linear objectives is governed by 'polyhedral instability' (number of active region changes), providing tight bounds that interpolate between experts and OCO rates.

entry.title: Tight Sample Complexity Bounds for Entropic Best Policy Identification

author.name: Amer Essakine, Claire Vernade

entry.summary: Closes the exponential gap in sample complexity for entropic best policy identification in risk-sensitive RL, matching the Ω(e^{|β|H}) lower bound by revisiting concentration analysis for exponential utilities.

entry.title: Orthrus: Memory-Efficient Parallel Token Generation via Dual-View Diffusion

author.name: Chien Van Nguyen, Chaitra Hegde, Van Cuong Pham, Ryan A. Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Thien Huu Nguyen

entry.summary: Introduces Orthrus, a dual-architecture framework combining frozen autoregressive LLMs with lightweight diffusion modules for parallel token generation, maintaining exact generation fidelity while achieving speedup.

entry.title: DP-Muon: Differentially Private Optimization via Matrix-Orthogonalized Momentum

author.name: Jihwan Kim, Chenglin Fan

entry.summary: DP-Muon adapts the Muon optimizer (which uses momentum and Newton-Schulz orthogonalization) for differential privacy training, proving that the orthogonalization step is post-processing and adds no privacy cost. This enables using advanced optimizers in privacy-preserving settings.

entry.title: JEDI: Joint Embedding Diffusion World Model for Online Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jing Yu Lim, Rushi Shah, Zarif Ikram, Samson Yu, Haozhe Ma, Tze-Yun Leong, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: JEDI combines JEPA-style representation learning with diffusion-based world modeling for online model-based RL, addressing the tension between pixel-space diffusion (effective but expensive) and latent diffusion (efficient but underperforming) approaches.

entry.title: Phasor Memory Networks: Stable Backpropagation Through Time for Scalable Explicit Memory

author.name: Sungwoo Goo, Hwi-yeol Yun, Sangkeun Jung

entry.summary: Phasor Memory Networks resolve the gradient instability of explicit memory architectures (like Neural Turing Machines) through unitary phasor dynamics on complex unit circles, enabling stable backpropagation through time for byte-level language modeling.

entry.title: Strategic PAC Learnability via Geometric Definability

author.name: Yuval Filmus, Shay Moran, Elizaveta Nesterova, Nir Rosenfeld, Alexander Shlimovich

entry.summary: Studies strategic PAC learnability where agents can modify features, showing that in general even VC-1 classes can have infinite induced complexity, then identifies geometric definability conditions that control complexity.

entry.title: Reducing cross-sample prediction churn in scientific machine learning

author.name: Gordan Prastalo, Kevin Maik Jablonka

entry.summary: Identifies and quantifies 'cross-sample prediction churn' in scientific ML—where models trained on different bootstrap samples of the same data disagree on 8-21.8% of test predictions despite similar aggregate accuracy. Shows data-side methods (bagging, conformal rejection) reduce churn while parameter-side methods don't.

entry.title: Dual-Pathway Circuits of Object Hallucination in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiaxin Liu, Ding Zhong, Yue Wang, Zhidong Yang, Zhaolu Kang, Guangyuan Dong, Qishi Zhan, Pengcheng Fang, Aofan Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Dual-Pathway Circuit Analysis to identify and characterize hallucination circuits in VLMs, discovering a visual grounding pathway and a hallucination pathway through activation patching across five architectures.

entry.title: Sustaining AI safety: Control-theoretic external impossibility, intrinsic necessity, and structural requirements

author.name: James M. Mazzu

entry.summary: Uses control theory to prove that external safety control becomes impossible once an AI system's effects exceed what bounded control can counteract, arguing that intrinsic safety properties become structurally necessary beyond a certain capability threshold.

entry.title: GRACE: Gradient-aligned Reasoning Data Curation for Efficient Post-training

author.name: Junjie Li, Ziao Wang, NingXuan Ma, Jianghong Ma, Xiaofeng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GRACE, a data curation method for reasoning model training that scores each reasoning step by its alignment with the answer-oriented gradient direction and consistency with the preceding trajectory, enabling efficient subset selection.

entry.title: VideoSEAL: Mitigating Evidence Misalignment in Agentic Long Video Understanding by Decoupling Answer Authority

author.name: Chenhao Qiu (Mango TV), Yechao Zhang (Nanyang Technological University), Xin Luo (Mango TV), Shien Song (Mango TV), Xusheng Liu (Mango TV)

entry.summary: Identifies 'evidence misalignment' in long video understanding agents where correct answers aren't supported by retrieved evidence. Introduces temporal and semantic groundedness diagnostics and proposes VideoSEAL to decouple answer authority between retriever and reasoner.

entry.title: Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation via Peer Successes and Failures

author.name: Weichen Yu, Xiaomin Li, Yizhou Zhao, Xiaoze Liu, Ruowang Zhang, Haixin Wang, Yinyi Luo, Chen Henry Wu, Gaurav Mittal, Matt Fredrikson, Yu Hu

entry.summary: Introduces MOPD (Multi-Rollout On-Policy Distillation), which conditions teacher signals on both successful and failed peer rollouts during distillation, providing denser supervision than independent per-rollout distillation.

entry.title: Uncovering Symmetry Transfer in Large Language Models via Layer-Peeled Optimization

author.name: Zhehang Du, Hangfeng He, Weijie Su

entry.summary: Analyzes how symmetries in target next-token distributions transfer to LLM weight geometry through layer-peeled optimization. Proves group-theoretic symmetry transfer in a tractable optimization surrogate for LLMs.

entry.title: Data Difficulty and the Generalization--Extrapolation Tradeoff in LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Siyuan Liu (IIIS, Tsinghua University), Tinghong Chen (College of AI, Tsinghua University, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute), Xinghan Li (IIIS, Tsinghua University), Yifei Wang (Amazon AGI SF Lab), Jingzhao Zhang (IIIS, Tsinghua University, Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute)

entry.summary: Studies the role of data difficulty in LLM fine-tuning, showing no universally optimal difficulty level - optimal difficulty depends on dataset size and shifts toward harder data as budget increases, with theoretical explanation via a generalization-extrapolation tradeoff.

entry.title: Understanding and Accelerating the Training of Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chunsan Hong, Sanghyun Lee, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Satoshi Hayakawa, Yuhta Takida, Yuki Mitsufuji, Seungryong Kim, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Analyzes why masked diffusion models (MDMs) train much more slowly than autoregressive models, identifying locality bias of language as the main factor. Proposes bell-shaped time sampling as a simple remedy to accelerate training while maintaining performance.

entry.title: N-vium: Mixture-of-Exits Transformer for Accelerated Exact Generation

author.name: Aleksander Lorenc, Fr\'ed\'eric Berdoz, Jo\"el Mathys, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: Introduces N-vium, a mixture-of-exits transformer that parallelizes computation across depth by defining the next-token distribution as a learned mixture over predictions from multiple depths. Increases effective FLOPs/second rather than minimizing compute per token.

entry.title: MinT: Managed Infrastructure for Training and Serving Millions of LLMs

author.name: Mind Lab, :, Song Cao, Vic Cao, Andrew Chen, Kaijie Chen, Cleon Cheng, Steven Chiang, Kaixuan Fan, Hera Feng, Huan Feng, Arthur Fu, Jun Gao, Hongquan Gu, Aaron Guan, Nolan Ho, Mutian Hong, Hailee Hou, Peixuan Hua, Charles Huang, Miles Jiang, Nora Jiang, Yuyi Jiang, Qiuyu Jin, Fancy Kong, Andrew Lei, Kyrie Lei, Alexy Li, Lucian Li, Ray Li, Theo Li, Zhihui Li, Jiayi Lin, Kairus Liu, Kieran Liu, Logan Liu, Xiang Liu, Irvine Lu, Maeve Luo, Runze Lv, Pony Ma, Verity Niu, Anson Qiu, Vincent Wang, Rio Yang, Maxwell Yao, Carrie Ye, Regis Ye, Wenlin Ye, Josh Ying, Danney Zeng, Yuhan Zhan, Anya Zhang, Di Zhang, Ruijia Zhang, Sueky Zhang, Ya Zhang, Wei Zhao, Ada Zhou, Changhai Zhou, Yuhua Zhou, Xinyue Zhu, Murphy Zhuang

entry.summary: Presents MinT, a managed infrastructure system for LoRA post-training and serving millions of LLM policies efficiently. Keeps base models resident and manages LoRA adapter lifecycles across training, evaluation, and serving, scaling to frontier-scale dense and MoE architectures.

entry.title: Early Data Exposure Improves Robustness to Subsequent Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lawrence Feng, Gaurav R. Ghosal, Jacob Mitchell Springer, Ziqian Zhong, Aditi Raghunathan

entry.summary: Studies how upstream training choices affect the robustness of capabilities to subsequent fine-tuning, finding that immediate post-training performance doesn't predict retention. Early data exposure during pretraining creates more robust capabilities across 135M and 1B models.

entry.title: Reinforced Collaboration in Multi-Agent Flow Networks

author.name: Zheng Wang, Yuang Liu, Yangkai Ding

entry.summary: MANGO is a framework that optimizes multi-agent LLM collaboration using flow networks built from past successful workflows, combining reinforcement learning with textual gradients to jointly optimize workflow paths and agent behaviors. This addresses error propagation in multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Collaborating in Multi-Armed Bandits with Strategic Agents

author.name: Idan Barnea, Ofir Schlisselberg, Yishay Mansour

entry.summary: Studies collaborative learning in multi-agent Bayesian bandits with strategic persistent agents who might free-ride on others' exploration. Proposes an information-sharing protocol that incentivizes exploration without monetary transfers.

entry.title: Continual Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models via Program Memory

author.name: Hung Le, Svetha Venkatesh

entry.summary: ProCL organizes LoRA adapters into structured program memory inspired by complementary learning systems in neuroscience, separating short-term adaptation from long-term knowledge consolidation for continual fine-tuning of LLMs.

entry.title: The Diffusion Encoder

author.name: Akhil Premkumar, Sarah Lucioni

entry.summary: Proposes the Diffusion Encoder, replacing VAE encoders with diffusion models using an alternating training scheme inspired by EM. Enables more expressive encoder distributions beyond what reparameterization trick allows.

entry.title: Rescaled Asynchronous SGD: Optimal Distributed Optimization under Data and System Heterogeneity

author.name: Ammar Mahran, Artavazd Maranjyan, Peter Richt\'arik

entry.summary: Proposes Rescaled ASGD that fixes the bias of vanilla asynchronous SGD toward faster workers under data heterogeneity by simple rescaling, achieving optimal rates without buffering, gathering, or extra memory.

entry.title: Provable Quantization with Randomized Hadamard Transform

author.name: Ying Feng, Piotr Indyk, Michael Kapralov, Dmitry Krachun, Boris Prokhorov

entry.summary: Provides rigorous theoretical guarantees for dithered quantization with randomized Hadamard transform, closing the gap between empirical success and theoretical understanding. Achieves O(d log d) time with provable compression bounds.

entry.title: LLMs as Implicit Imputers: Uncertainty Should Scale with Missing Information

author.name: Stef van Buuren

entry.summary: Argues that LLMs operating under incomplete context are implicit imputors and evaluates whether their uncertainty scales appropriately with missing information. Finds confidence fails to reflect missingness while entropy partially succeeds.

entry.title: Characterizing Universal Object Representations Across Vision Models

author.name: Florian P. Mahner, Johannes Roth, Ka Chun Lam, Michael F. Bonner, Francisco Pereira, Martin N. Hebart

entry.summary: Decomposes object similarity structure across 162 diverse vision models into non-negative dimensions to identify universal vs model-specific representations. Finds universal dimensions are more interpretable and driven by conceptual/semantic properties.

entry.title: PRISM-X: Experiments on Personalised Fine-Tuning with Human and Simulated Users

author.name: Hannah Rose Kirk, Liu Leqi, Fanzhi Zeng, Henry Davidson, Bertie Vidgen, Christopher Summerfield, Scott A. Hale

entry.summary: Large-scale within-subject experiment (530 participants from 52 countries) comparing personalized and non-personalized LLMs, finding preference fine-tuning outperforms prompting and revealing gaps between simulated and real users.

entry.title: Learning to See What You Need: Gaze Attention for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Junha Song, Byeongho Heo, Geonmo Gu, Jaegul Choo, Dongyoon Han, Sangdoo Yun

entry.summary: Introduces Gaze Attention mechanism for multimodal LLMs that selectively attends to task-relevant visual regions during generation, mimicking human selective fixation. Reduces computational overhead while improving focus.

entry.title: MindVLA-U1: VLA Beats VA with Unified Streaming Architecture for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Yuzhou Huang, Benjin Zhu, Hengtong Lu, Victor Shea-Jay Huang, Haiming Zhang, Wei Chen, Jifeng Dai, Yan Xie, Hongsheng Li

entry.summary: MindVLA-U1 presents the first unified streaming VLA architecture for autonomous driving that integrates language reasoning with continuous control, demonstrating VLA can surpass vision-to-action models on planning quality.

entry.title: Predicting Rare LLM Failures with 30× Fewer Rollouts

author.name: Santiago Aranguri

entry.summary: Introduces Logit Path Extrapolation, which interpolates between a safety-trained model and a less-safe variant in logit space to predict rare harmful behaviors with 30x fewer evaluation rollouts than naive sampling.

entry.title: F-GRPO: Factorized Group-Relative Policy Optimization for Unified Candidate Generation and Ranking

author.name: Rohan Surana, Gagan Mundada, Junda Wu, Xintong Li, Yizhu Jiao, Bowen Jin, Sizhe Zhou, Tong Yu, Ritwik Sinha, Jiawei Han, Jingbo Shang, Julian McAuley

entry.summary: F-GRPO addresses the credit assignment problem in LLM-based retrieval by factorizing the generation of ranked lists into candidate selection and ranking components, enabling separate optimization of each via group-relative policy optimization.

entry.title: Switching Successor Measures for Hierarchical Zero-shot Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Stefan Stojanovic, Alexandre Proutiere

entry.summary: Introduces switching successor measures for hierarchical zero-shot RL, enabling hierarchical control without additional supervision, fixed horizons, or manually designed subgoals while preserving the theoretical properties of successor measures.

entry.title: Rethinking Generalization in Graph Neural Networks: A Structural Complexity Perspective

author.name: Peiyao Wang, Liang Bai, Xian Yang, Richard Yi Da Xu, Jiye Liang

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of how graph structure influences GNN generalization, proving that incorporating structural information improves generalization bounds and proposing a structural complexity measure for evaluation.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Evaluating Prospective Metacognitive Control in LLMs under Resource Constraints

author.name: Zabir Al Nazi, Shubhashis Roy Dipta

entry.summary: Introduces TRIAGE, an evaluation framework testing whether LLMs can perform prospective metacognitive control—deciding which tasks to attempt, in what order, and how much compute to allocate—under finite token budgets.

entry.title: How to Interpret Agent Behavior

author.name: Jie Gao, Kaiser Sun, Jen-tse Huang, Katherine Van Koevering, Sijie Ji, Heyuan Huang, Weiyan Shi, Zhuoran Lu, Ziang Xiao, Daniel Khashabi, Mark Dredze

entry.summary: Introduces ACT*ONOMY, a three-level taxonomy for describing and analyzing autonomous agent behavior at runtime, developed through Grounded Theory analysis of reasoning trajectories from Claude Code and Codex.

entry.title: Agentic Interpretation: Lattice-Structured Evidence for LLM-Based Program Analysis

author.name: Jacqueline L. Mitchell, Chao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes agentic interpretation, a framework that structures LLM-based program analysis using lattice-structured evidence, enabling incremental, auditable analysis that leverages documentation and security advisories beyond source code.

entry.title: Discrete MeanFlow: One-Step Generation via Conditional Transition Kernels

author.name: Fairoz Nower Khan, Nabuat Zaman Nahim, Md Sajid Ahmed, Ruiquan Huang, Peizhong Ju

entry.summary: Extends MeanFlow to discrete state spaces by replacing continuous trajectories with probability mass transport over finite states. Proves a Discrete MeanFlow identity relating finite-interval rates to instantaneous CTMC rates, enabling one-step generation.

entry.title: Persona-Model Collapse in Emergent Misalignment

author.name: Davi Bastos Costa, Renato Vicente

entry.summary: Proposes that emergent misalignment involves persona-model collapse - deterioration of the model's capacity to differentiate and maintain consistent characters. Tests with moral susceptibility and robustness metrics using Moral Foundations Questionnaire.

entry.title: Inducing Overthink: Hierarchical Genetic Algorithm-based DoS Attack on Black-Box Large Language Reasoning Models

author.name: Shuqiang Wang, Wei Cao, Jiaqi Weng, Jialing Tao, Licheng Pan, Hui Xue, Zhixuan Chu

entry.summary: Investigates DoS-style attacks on Large Reasoning Models by systematically perturbing input logic to induce overthinking (excessively long reasoning traces), using a hierarchical genetic algorithm as a black-box attack framework.

entry.title: High-Rate Quantized Matrix Multiplication II

author.name: Or Ordentlich, Yury Polyanskiy

entry.summary: Investigates quantized matrix multiplication with available covariance information, showing how waterfilling from rate-distortion theory can improve practical LLM quantization algorithms like GPTQ by optimally distributing bit-rate across weight coordinates rather than allocating equally.

entry.title: The Efficiency Gap in Byte Modeling

author.name: Celine Lee, Jing Nathan Yan, Chen Liang, Jiaxin Shi, Yin Zhang, Jeremiah Liu, Pengcheng Yin, Fernando Pereira, Ed Chi, Derek Cheng, Alexander M. Rush, Ruoxi Wang

entry.summary: Investigates the efficiency gap of byte-level modeling compared to subword tokenization through compute-matched scaling studies, also examining masked diffusion vs. autoregressive generation. Finds significant but potentially addressable computational penalties for removing structural priors.

entry.title: Mix, Don't Tune: Bilingual Pre-Training Outperforms Hyperparameter Search in Data-Constrained Settings

author.name: Paul Jeha, Anastasiia Sedova, Louis B\'ethune, Skyler Seto, Jes Frellsen, Pierre Ablin, Natalie Schluter

entry.summary: Shows that bilingual pre-training (mixing data from a high-resource language) outperforms aggressive hyperparameter tuning for data-constrained language model pre-training, with systematic comparisons across four model scales.

entry.title: Path-independent Flow Matching for Multi-parameter Generative Dynamics

author.name: Francisco T\'ellez, AmirHossein Zamani, Philippe Martin, Shuang Ni, Guy Wolf, Eugene Belilovsky, Sina Sanjari, Yanlei Zhang

entry.summary: PiFM extends flow matching to multi-parameter domains while enforcing path independence, ensuring transport depends only on initial and target distributions rather than the specific path taken.

entry.title: Sampling from Flow Language Models via Marginal-Conditioned Bridges

author.name: Iskander Azangulov, Leo Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that the natural sampler for Flow Language Models is posterior-predictive rather than DDPM-style, sampling clean one-hot endpoints from token marginals before bridging, improving generation quality.

entry.title: On the Generalization of Knowledge Distillation: An Information-Theoretic View

author.name: Bingying Li, Haiyun He

entry.summary: Provides information-theoretic generalization bounds for knowledge distillation, modeling teacher and student training as coupled stochastic processes and introducing a 'distillation divergence' measure. Derives both upper and lower bounds.

entry.title: Proximal-Based Generative Modeling for Bayesian Inverse Problems

author.name: Boyang Zhang, Zhiguo Wang, Ya-Feng Liu

entry.summary: Proposes proximal-based generative modeling (PGM) that replaces intractable likelihood scores in diffusion-based inverse problems with Moreau scores computable via proximal operators, establishing theoretical equivalence between Gaussian convolution and Moreau-Yosida regularization.

entry.title: No One Knows the State of the Art in Geospatial Foundation Models

author.name: Isaac Corley, Nils Lehmann, Caleb Robinson, Gabriel Tseng, Anthony Fuller, Hamed Alemohammad, Evan Shelhamer, Jennifer Marcus, Hannah Kerner

entry.summary: Audits 152 geospatial foundation model papers finding 46 cross-paper disagreements of 10+ points for the same model/benchmark, arguing nobody can reliably determine SOTA due to lack of standardization.

entry.title: Structural Diversity Drives Disruptive Scientific Innovation

author.name: Yichun Peng, Saike He, Peijie Zhang, Kang Zhao, Yi Yang, Ning Zhang, Qingpeng Zhang, Daniel Dajun Zeng, Hao Peng

entry.summary: Introduces Structural Diversity metric measuring how teams bridge knowledge communities, showing it robustly predicts disruptive scientific innovation using 260 million publications (1900-2025) with causal validation.

entry.title: A Research Agenda for Secret Loyalties

author.name: Joe Kwon

entry.summary: Defines and analyzes 'secret loyalties' - when AI models are intentionally caused to advance a specific actor's interests without disclosure. Proposes a research agenda addressing this threat as AI systems gain more responsibilities in military, scientific, and coding applications.

entry.title: Teaching and Learning under Deductive Errors

author.name: Jan Arne Telle, Brigt H{\aa}vardstun, Jose Hernandez-Orallo

entry.summary: Introduces a PAC teaching/learning framework that accounts for deductive errors in learners, relevant to humans and LLMs in few-shot settings where consistency checks can fail stochastically.

entry.title: Mixed neural posterior estimation for simulators with discrete and continuous parameters

author.name: Jan Boelts, Cornelius Schr\"oder, Jonas Beck, Jakob H. Macke, Michael Deistler, Daniel Gedon

entry.summary: Extends Neural Posterior Estimation to mixed (discrete + continuous) parameter spaces by factorizing the joint posterior into discrete and continuous components, using autoregressive classifiers and generative models respectively.

entry.title: DisaBench: A Participatory Evaluation Framework for Disability Harms in Language Models

author.name: Eugenia Kim, Ioana Tanase, Christina Mallon

entry.summary: Introduces DisaBench, a disability-focused safety benchmark for LLMs co-created with people with disabilities, featuring a taxonomy of 12 harm categories, 175 prompts, and human-annotated evaluations revealing that harm rates vary sharply by disability type.

entry.title: Beyond Cooperative Simulators: Generating Realistic User Personas for Robust Evaluation of LLM Agents

author.name: Harshita Chopra, Kshitish Ghate, Aylin Caliskan, Tadayoshi Kohno, Chirag Shah, Natasha Jaques

entry.summary: Introduces Persona Policies (PPol), a plug-and-play control layer that makes LLM-based user simulators exhibit realistic behavioral variation (unclear, impatient, reluctant users) rather than being uniformly cooperative, improving agent evaluation.

entry.title: What properties of reasoning supervision are associated with improved downstream model quality?

author.name: Miko{\l}aj Langner, Dzmitry Pihulski, Jan Eliasz, Micha{\l} Rajkowski, Przemys{\l}aw Kazienko, Maciej Piasecki, Jan Koco\'n, Teddy Ferdinan

entry.summary: Investigates whether the utility of reasoning training data can be predicted before fine-tuning using intrinsic data metrics, finding strong correlations with downstream performance that are scale-dependent.

entry.title: VERA-MH: Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health

author.name: Luca Belli, Kate H. Bentley, Josh Gieringer, Emily Van Ark, Nilu Zhao, Pradip Thachile, Matt Hawrilenko, Millard Brown, Adam M. Chekroud

entry.summary: Introduces VERA-MH, a clinically-validated evaluation for chatbot safety in mental health contexts, focusing on suicidal ideation risks through conversation simulation with clinician-designed personas and expert-judged outcomes.

entry.title: ODRPO: Ordinal Decompositions of Discrete Rewards for Robust Policy Optimization

author.name: Nirmal Patel, Fei Wang, Inderjit Dhillon

entry.summary: Addresses stochasticity in LLM auto-raters for RLAIF by proposing ODRPO, which decomposes discrete multi-tier rewards into ordinal components to create more robust advantage estimators that resist noisy reward signals.

entry.title: MMCL-Bench: Multimodal Context Learning from Visual Rules, Procedures, and Evidence

author.name: Yifan Chen, Fei Yin, Qingyan Bai, Zicheng Lin, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Introduces MMCL-Bench, a benchmark for multimodal context learning requiring models to learn rules, procedures, and patterns from visual teaching context and apply them to new instances. Current frontier models perform poorly.

entry.title: Inline Critic Steers Image Editing

author.name: Weitai Kang, Xiaohang Zhan, Yizhou Wang, Mang Tik Chiu, Jason Kuen, Kangning Liu, Yan Yan

entry.summary: Introduces Inline Critic, a learnable token that critiques a frozen image-editing model's predictions at an intermediate layer during the forward pass, enabling within-pass refinement rather than post-generation correction.

entry.title: The Expressivity Boundary of Probabilistic Circuits: A Comparison with Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiyu Zhao, Xuejie Liu, Muhan Zhang, Anji Liu

entry.summary: Identifies output and context-encoding bottlenecks limiting probabilistic circuits vs LLMs for language modeling. Shows logit-space parameterization narrows the gap, and proves structured-decomposable PCs can match Transformer separation rank on aligned partitions.

entry.title: Watermarking Should Be Treated as a Monitoring Primitive

author.name: Toluwani Aremu, Nils Lukas, Jie Zhang

entry.summary: Argues that watermarking for generative models should be treated as a monitoring primitive, introducing an observer-based threat model where aggregating watermark signals across outputs can reveal entity-level information even from zero-bit schemes.

entry.title: Beyond Perplexity: A Geometric and Spectral Study of Low-Rank Pre-Training

author.name: Namrata Shivagunde, Vijeta Deshpande, Sherin Muckatira, Anna Rumshisky

entry.summary: Goes beyond perplexity to characterize low-rank pre-training through geometric and spectral analysis of loss landscapes and internal representations. Reveals that low-rank methods can match full-rank perplexity while converging to fundamentally different solutions, questioning perplexity as the sole evaluation metric.

entry.title: KVServe: Service-Aware KV Cache Compression for Communication-Efficient Disaggregated LLM Serving

author.name: Zedong Liu, Xinyang Ma, Dejun Luo, Hairui Zhao, Bing Lu, Wenjing Huang, Yida Gu, Xingchen Liu, Zheng Wei, Jinyang Liu, Dingwen Tao, Guangming Tan

entry.summary: Presents KVServe, the first service-aware adaptive KV cache compression framework for disaggregated LLM serving that dynamically adjusts compression based on workload mix, bandwidth, and SLO budgets. Unifies multiple KV compression strategies into a single adaptive system.

entry.title: U-HNO: A U-shaped Hybrid Neural Operator with Sparse-Point Adaptive Routing for Non-stationary PDE Dynamics

author.name: Yingzhe Ma, Xiao Yang, Yuxin Xie, Zihan Xiong, Jinliang Liu

entry.summary: U-HNO is a U-shaped hybrid neural operator that adaptively combines Fourier-based and spatially local architectures via sparse-point routing, addressing the tension between capturing global transport and resolving localized sharp features in PDE solutions.

entry.title: Bayesian Nonparametric Mixed-Effect ODEs with Gaussian Processes

author.name: Julien Martinelli, Maksim Sinelnikov, Harri L\"ahdesm\"aki, Quentin Clairon, M\'elanie Prague

entry.summary: Develops Bayesian nonparametric mixed-effect ODE models using Gaussian processes, allowing different subjects to follow related but distinct continuous-time dynamics without specifying parametric vector fields, addressing structural misspecification in domains like pharmacometrics.

entry.title: GeoFlowVLM: Geometry-Aware Joint Uncertainty for Frozen Vision-Language Embedding

author.name: Mayank Nautiyal, Li Ju, Andreas Hellander, Ekta Vats, Prashant Singh

entry.summary: GeoFlowVLM adds post-hoc uncertainty quantification to frozen vision-language model embeddings using Riemannian flow matching on product hyperspheres, capturing both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty.

entry.title: EGSS: Entropy-guided Stepwise Scaling for Reliable Software Engineering

author.name: Chenhui Mao, Yuanting Lei, Zhixiang Wei, Ming Liang, Zhixiang Wang, Jingxuan Xu, Dajun Chen, Wei Jiang, Yong Li

entry.summary: Proposes EGSS, an entropy-guided test-time scaling framework for software engineering tasks that dynamically balances computational efficiency with effectiveness through adaptive search and test-suite augmentation. Addresses the high cost of agentic test-time scaling.

entry.title: DocAtlas: Multilingual Document Understanding Across 80+ Languages

author.name: Ahmed Heakl, Youssef Mohamed, Abdullah Sohail, Rania Elbadry, Ahmed Nassar, Peter W. J. Staar, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Imran Razzak, Salman Khan

entry.summary: Introduces DocAtlas, a framework constructing high-fidelity OCR datasets and benchmarks covering 82 languages and 9 tasks for multilingual document understanding. Evaluates 16 SOTA models and reveals persistent gaps in low-resource scripts, showing DPO can help.

entry.title: Code-Centric Detection of Vulnerability-Fixing Commits: A Unified Benchmark and Empirical Study

author.name: Nils Loose, Joseph Bienh\"uls, Kristoffer Hempel, Felix M\"achtle, Thomas Eisenbarth

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive evaluation of code language models for vulnerability-fixing commit (VFC) detection across 180K+ commits. Finds models don't acquire transferable security understanding from code changes alone—commit messages dominate when available.

entry.title: GAGPO: Generalized Advantage Grouped Policy Optimization

author.name: Siyuan Zhu, Chao Yu, Rongxin Yang, Zongkai Liu, Jinjun Hu, Qiwen Chen, Yibo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes GAGPO, a critic-free RL method for LLM agents that provides step-aligned temporal credit assignment in multi-turn environments using a non-parametric grouped value proxy from sampled rollouts.

entry.title: Hierarchical Transformer Preconditioning for Interactive Physics Simulation

author.name: Carl Osborne, Minghao Guo, Crystal Owens, Wojciech Matusik

entry.summary: Introduces Hierarchical Transformer Preconditioner for physics simulation, anchored to H-matrix partitions for O(N) approximate-inverse computation. Uses highway connections for long-range coupling with interactive-rate performance.

entry.title: Limits of Personalizing Differential Privacy Budgets

author.name: Edwige Cyffers, Juba Ziani

entry.summary: Shows that personalized differential privacy budgets have limited advantage over a simple thresholding operator for mean estimation. Precisely quantifies the constant-factor improvement from full personalization.

entry.title: What is Learnable in Valiant's Theory of the Learnable?

author.name: Steve Hanneke, Anay Mehrotra, Grigoris Velegkas, Manolis Zampetakis

entry.summary: Revisits Valiant's original 1984 learning model (positive examples + membership queries, no false positives) and characterizes learnable classes via adaptive query-compression schemes, providing a new variant of sample compression.

entry.title: Prefix Teach, Suffix Fade: Local Teachability Collapse in Strong-to-Weak On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kaiyuan Liu, Ziyuan Zhuang, Yang Bai, Bing Wang, Rongxiang Weng, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Identifies 'local teachability collapse' in strong-to-weak on-policy distillation where later trajectory segments lack local contrast for effective learning, proposing to concentrate supervision on earlier, more teachable regions.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic Lifelong LLM Safety via Externalized Attack-Defense Co-Evolution

author.name: Xiaozhe Zhang, Chaozhuo Li, Hui Liu, Shaocheng Yan, Bingyu Yan, Qiwei Ye, Haoliang Li

entry.summary: Proposes EvoSafety, a model-agnostic LLM safety framework with externalized adversarial skill libraries and guardrail skill libraries that can evolve independently and transfer across models.

entry.title: Pyramid Forcing: Head-Aware Pyramid KV Cache Policy for High-Quality Long Video Generation

author.name: Jiayu Chen, Junbei Tang, Wenbiao Zhao, Maoliang Li, Jiayi Luo, Zihao Zheng, Jiawei Yang, Guojie Luo, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Pyramid Forcing identifies three distinct attention head types (Anchor, Wave, Veil) in autoregressive video generation and assigns head-specific KV cache policies for long video generation without quality degradation.

entry.title: Training Long-Context Vision-Language Models Effectively with Generalization Beyond 128K Context

author.name: Zhaowei Wang, Lishu Luo, Haodong Duan, Weiwei Liu, Sijin Wu, Ji Luo, Shen Yan, Shuai Peng, Sihang Yuan, Chaoyi Huang, Yi Lin, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Systematic study of long-context continued pretraining for vision-language models, extending 7B model to 128K context with findings that long-document VQA is more effective than OCR transcription for training.

entry.title: Action Emergence from Streaming Intent

author.name: Pengfei Jing, Victor Shea-Jay Huang, Hengtong Lu, Jifeng Dai, Xie Yan, Benjin Zhu

entry.summary: Formalizes action emergence for autonomous driving—generating feasible actions in long-tail scenes through reasoning rather than retrieval—and proposes Streaming Intent as a mechanism making driving intent steerable and temporally continuous.

entry.title: Claude is Now Alignment-Pretrained

author.name: RogerDearnaley

entry.summary: Discusses Anthropic's adoption of alignment pretraining - using SGD on documents showing AI doing the right thing in morally challenging situations. The author has been advocating this approach for years and sees it as vindication of the technique.

entry.title: Retrieval is Cheap, Show Me the Code: Executable Multi-Hop Reasoning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Jiashuo Sun, Jimeng Shi, Yixuan Xie, Saizhuo Wang, Jash Rajesh Parekh, Pengcheng Jiang, Zhiyi Shi, Jiajun Fan, Qinglong Zheng, Peiran Li, Shaowen Wang, Ge Liu, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: Proposes using code generation rather than natural language for multi-hop RAG reasoning, where intermediate states are explicit program variables rather than implicit text, enabling grounded self-reflection and reducing error propagation.

entry.title: \emph{DRIFT}: A Benchmark for Task-Free Continual Graph Learning with Continuous Distribution Shifts

author.name: Guiquan Sun, Xikun Zhang, Jingchao Ni, Dongjin Song

entry.summary: DRIFT is a benchmark for task-free continual graph learning with continuous distribution shifts, modeling data streams as time-varying mixtures of latent task distributions rather than discrete task boundaries. Provides a more realistic evaluation setting for continual learning on graphs.

entry.title: Unified generalization analysis for physics informed neural networks

author.name: Yuka Hashimoto, Tomoharu Iwata

entry.summary: Provides unified generalization bounds for PINNs and VPINNs using Taylor expansion to represent nonlinear differential operators as linear operators on high-dimensional spaces, enabling Koopman-based analysis without restrictive stability assumptions.

entry.title: Beyond Oversquashing: Understanding Signal Propagation in GNNs Via Observables

author.name: Eden Nagar, Ya-Wei Eileen Lin, Ron Levie

entry.summary: Proposes a quantum mechanics-inspired framework using observables to model signal propagation in GNNs, offering an alternative to oversquashing/oversmoothing perspectives that tracks where signal lies, its concentration, and propagation.

entry.title: Before the Last Token: Diagnosing Final-Token Safety Probe Failures

author.name: Shravan Doda

entry.summary: Diagnoses failure modes of final-token safety probes against jailbreaks, showing that while probes work well on clean harmful prompts, they miss jailbreaks where unsafe evidence is distributed across earlier token representations. Increasing probe width doesn't reliably help.

entry.title: Revisiting DAgger in the Era of LLM-Agents

author.name: Changhao Li, Rushi Qiang, Jiawei Huang, Chenxiao Gao, Chao Zhang, Niao He, Bo Dai

entry.summary: Revisits Dataset Aggregation (DAgger) for multi-turn LLM agents, using turn-level interpolation of student and teacher policies to address covariate shift while maintaining dense teacher supervision. Bridges supervised fine-tuning and RL approaches.

entry.title: LightSplit: Practical Privacy-Preserving Split Learning via Orthogonal Projections

author.name: Mert Cihangiroglu, Alessandro Pegoraro, Phillip Rieger, Antonino Nocera, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi

entry.summary: LightSplit uses fixed orthogonal random projections at the split learning cut layer to simultaneously reduce communication overhead and protect against reconstruction attacks, grounded in Shannon information theory.
