entry.summary: Proposes 'Rollout Cards' as a reproducibility standard for agent research after auditing 50 repositories and finding none report failed/errored/skipped runs. Documents 37 cases where reporting rules change task-success metrics for fixed evidence.

entry.title: Reinforcing VLAs in Task-Agnostic World Models

author.name: Yucen Wang, Rui Yu, Fengming Zhang, Junjie Lu, Xinyao Qin, Tianxiang Zhang, Kaixin Wang, Li Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes RAW-Dream, a paradigm for reinforcing Vision-Language-Action models using task-agnostic world models that capture transferable physical priors for zero-shot inference, completely disentangling world model learning from downstream tasks.

entry.title: RT-Transformer: The Transformer Block as a Spherical State Estimator

author.name: Peter Racioppo

entry.summary: Shows that transformer block components (attention, residual connections, normalization) arise naturally from modeling latent state as a direction on the hypersphere with tangent-plane noise, yielding a precision-weighted directional inference procedure.

entry.title: Sequential Behavioral Watermarking for LLM Agents

author.name: Hyeseon An, Shinwoo Park, Dongsu Kim, Yo-Sub Han

entry.summary: Introduces sequential behavioral watermarking for LLM agents that embeds provenance signals in action trajectories rather than generated text. Accounts for trajectory structure to remain robust under perturbation and truncation.

entry.title: The Scaling Law of Evaluation Failure: Why Simple Averaging Collapses Under Data Sparsity and Item Difficulty Gaps, and How Item Response Theory Recovers Ground Truth Across Domains

author.name: Jung Min Kang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that simple averaging in benchmark evaluation produces misleading rankings under data sparsity and item difficulty heterogeneity. Shows Item Response Theory recovers ground truth across domains.

entry.title: Internalizing Curriculum Judgment for LLM Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

author.name: Han Zheng, Yining Ma, Karthick Gunasekaran, Bharathan Balaji, Zheng Du, Shiv Vitaladevuni, Cathy Wu

entry.summary: METIS internalizes curriculum judgment for LLM reinforcement fine-tuning by predicting within-prompt reward variance as a measure of prompt informativeness, using in-context learning examples.

entry.title: Discovery of Interpretable Surrogates via Agentic AI: Application to Gravitational Waves

author.name: Tousif Islam, Digvijay Wadekar, Tejaswi Venumadhav, Matias Zaldarriaga, Ajit Kumar Mehta, Javier Roulet, Barak Zackay

entry.summary: GWAgent uses an LLM-based agentic workflow to construct interpretable analytic surrogates for gravitational waveforms from simulation data. Shows physics-informed domain ansatz substantially improves accuracy.

entry.title: Gradient-Free Noise Optimization for Reward Alignment in Generative Models

author.name: Jeongsol Kim, Hongeun Kim, Jian Wang, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: ZeNO performs gradient-free noise optimization for reward alignment in generative models by formulating it as path-integral control. Works with non-differentiable rewards and deterministic generators.

entry.title: fg-expo: Frontier-guided exploration-prioritized policy optimization via adaptive kl and gaussian curriculum

author.name: Mingxiong Lin, Zhangquan Gong, Maowen Tang, Qian Li, Chuangchuang Wang, Jian Ma, Sutian Huang, Kai Tang, Haonan Lu

entry.summary: FG-ExPO improves GRPO for LLM math reasoning with accuracy-conditioned KL scaling (adaptive exploration) and Gaussian curriculum (targeting moderately difficult problems for informative gradients).

entry.title: Deep Minds and Shallow Probes

author.name: Su Hyeong Lee, Risi Kondor

entry.summary: Studies the mathematical foundations of neural representation probes, showing that probe families should be stable under representation symmetries. Derives a hierarchy of coordinate-stable probes with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Sharpen Your Flow: Sharpness-Aware Sampling for Flow Matching

author.name: Aditi Gupta, Soon Hoe Lim, Annan Yu, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: Proposes SharpEuler, a training-free sampler for flow matching models that allocates integration steps where the velocity field changes most rapidly, using offline sharpness profiling.

entry.title: Martingale-Consistent Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Moritz G\"ogl, Hanwen Xing, Christopher Yau

entry.summary: Introduces martingale-consistent self-supervised learning that enforces coherence between predictions from coarse and refined views, preventing systematic drift as information is revealed.

entry.title: IPI-proxy: An Intercepting Proxy for Red-Teaming Web-Browsing AI Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection

author.name: Chia-Pei (Janet), Chen, Kentaroh Toyoda, Anita Lai, Alex Leung

entry.summary: Presents IPI-proxy, a red-teaming toolkit for testing web-browsing AI agents against indirect prompt injection by rewriting HTTP responses from whitelisted domains in flight.

entry.title: L2P: Unlocking Latent Potential for Pixel Generation

author.name: Zhennan Chen, Junwei Zhu, Xu Chen, Jiangning Zhang, Jiawei Chen, Zhuoqi Zeng, Wei Zhang, Chengjie Wang, Jian Yang, Ying Tai

entry.summary: Proposes Latent-to-Pixel (L2P) transfer, converting pre-trained latent diffusion models to pixel-space models by replacing VAE with patch tokenization and training only shallow layers on synthetic data.

entry.title: Boosting Omni-Modal Language Models: Staged Post-Training with Visually Debiased Evaluation

author.name: Che Liu, Lichao Ma, Xiangyu Tony Zhang, Yuxin Zhang, Haoyang Zhang, Xuerui Yang, Fei Tian

entry.summary: Identifies that omni-modal (audio-visual-language) benchmarks are inflated by visual shortcuts, creates OmniClean (filtered benchmark), and proposes OmniBoost, a three-stage post-training pipeline. Audits 9 benchmarks and retains 8,551 of 16,968 queries.

entry.title: CIDR: A Large-Scale Industrial Source Code Dataset for Software Engineering Research

author.name: Vladislav Savenkov

entry.summary: Presents CIDR, a large-scale dataset of 2,440 proprietary industrial repositories (373M lines of code, 138 languages) collected from 12 partner organizations for software engineering research.

entry.title: Detecting overfitting in Neural Networks during long-horizon grokking using Random Matrix Theory

author.name: Hari K. Prakash, Charles H Martin

entry.summary: Presents a Random Matrix Theory method to detect overfitting without access to train/test data by identifying 'Correlation Traps'—outliers violating self-averaging in randomized weight matrix spectra during training.

entry.title: A Causal Language Modeling Detour Improves Encoder Continued Pretraining

author.name: Rian Touchent, Eric de la Clergerie

entry.summary: Shows that temporarily switching from MLM to CLM during encoder continued pretraining, followed by MLM decay, improves downstream performance. CLM impacts low transformer layers much more than MLM does.

entry.title: The Algorithmic Caricature: Auditing LLM-Generated Political Discourse Across Crisis Events

author.name: Gunjan, Sidahmed Benabderrahmane, Talal Rahwan

entry.summary: Audits LLM-generated political discourse across 9 crisis events (1.7M posts), finding systematic differences from real discourse including reduced emotional granularity and exaggerated polarization—'algorithmic caricature' of political views.

entry.title: Fast MoE Inference via Predictive Prefetching and Expert Replication

author.name: Ankit Jyothish, Ali Jannesari, Aishwarya Sarkar, Joseph Zuber

entry.summary: Proposes predictive prefetching and dynamic expert replication for MoE inference, predicting overloaded experts and replicating them to process tokens concurrently across GPUs.

entry.title: More Edits, More Stable: Understanding the Lifelong Normalization in Sequential Model Editing

author.name: Xin Ma, Wei Chen, Qi Liu, Derong Xu, Zhi Zheng, Tong Xu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of Lifelong Normalization in sequential model editing, explaining why it prevents collapse and discovering a counter-intuitive positive cumulative effect where early edits help future ones.

entry.title: Beyond Parameter Aggregation: Semantic Consensus for Federated Fine-Tuning of LLMs

author.name: Amr Abourayya, Jens Kleesiek, Michael Kamp

entry.summary: Proposes federated fine-tuning of LLMs through semantic consensus rather than parameter aggregation, where clients exchange generated outputs on shared prompts and the server aggregates in semantic space.

entry.title: Targeted Neuron Modulation via Contrastive Pair Search

author.name: Sam Herring, Jake Naviasky, Karan Malhotra

entry.summary: Introduces contrastive neuron attribution (CNA) to identify the 0.1% of MLP neurons that distinguish harmful from benign prompts in instruction-tuned LLMs, requiring only forward passes. Ablating this circuit reduces refusal rates by >50% while preserving fluency, revealing the refusal mechanism.

entry.title: Routers Learn the Geometry of Their Experts: Geometric Coupling in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Sagi Ahrac, Noya Hochwald, Mor Geva

entry.summary: Reveals geometric coupling between routers and experts in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models: matched router-expert pairs accumulate the same routed token history because their gradients share the same input direction. Uses this insight to improve routing and training.

entry.title: Training-Inference Consistent Segmented Execution for Long-Context LLMs

author.name: Xianpeng Shang, Jiang Li, Zehua Duo, Qianyi Cai, Xiangdong Su

entry.summary: Proposes a training-inference consistent segment-level generation framework for long-context LLMs, where both training and inference follow the same segment-level execution semantics. Addresses the mismatch between full-context training and bounded-context inference in current approaches.

entry.title: Variance-aware Reward Modeling with Anchor Guidance

author.name: Shuxing Fang, Ruijian Han, Liangyu Zhang, Fan Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Anchor-guided Variance-aware Reward Modeling that resolves non-identifiability in Gaussian reward models by adding two coarse response-level anchor labels. Proves two anchors suffice for identification and establishes convergence rates.

entry.title: Robust LLM Unlearning Against Relearning Attacks: The Minor Components in Representations Matter

author.name: Zeguan Xiao, Xuanzhe Xu, Yun Chen, Yong Wang, Jian Yang, Yanqing Hu, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: Investigates LLM unlearning robustness against relearning attacks from a representation geometry perspective. Discovers that existing methods modify dominant components but leave minor components unchanged, which enable rapid knowledge recovery during attacks.

entry.title: Combining On-Policy Optimization and Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Miguel Moura Ramos, Duarte M. Alves, Andr\'e F. T. Martins

entry.summary: Proposes combining on-policy reinforcement learning (GRPO) with knowledge distillation for adapting LLMs to long-context tasks, addressing exposure bias and sparse rewards that plague existing approaches individually.

entry.title: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues

author.name: Di Wu, Zixiang Ji, Asmi Kawatkar, Bryan Kwan, Jia-Chen Gu, Nanyun Peng, Kai-Wei Chang

entry.summary: Introduces LongMemEval-V2, a benchmark evaluating whether memory systems help web agents internalize environment-specific experience, with 451 questions covering five core memory abilities. From UCLA/Peng/Chang group.

entry.title: StepCodeReasoner: Aligning Code Reasoning with Stepwise Execution Traces via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hao Wang, Rui Li, Lei Sha, Jie M. Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes StepCodeReasoner, which aligns code reasoning with stepwise execution traces via RL, introducing Bi-Level GRPO for structured credit assignment at inter-trajectory and intra-trajectory levels.

entry.title: Beyond Masks: The Case for Medical Image Parsing

author.name: Siddharth Gupta, Alan L. Yuille, Zongwei Zhou

entry.summary: Argues that medical imaging should shift from per-voxel mask outputs to structured 'medical image parsing'—emitting entities, attributes, and relationships as structured representations matching radiologist reporting.

entry.title: Self-Consistent Latent Reasoning: Long Latent Sequence Reasoning for Vision-Language Model

author.name: Chenfeng Wang, Wei He, Xuhan Zhu, Chunpeng Zhou, Qizhen Li, Song Yan, Yufei Zheng, Chengjun Yu, Fan Lu, Wei Zhai, Yang Cao, Pengfei Yu, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: Discovers 'Information Gain Collapse' in visual latent reasoning: longer latent sequences degrade performance because autoregressive generation makes tokens highly dependent on prior outputs, adding no new information. Proposes self-consistent latent reasoning to fix this.

entry.title: Coordinated Diffusion: Generating Multi-Agent Behavior Without Multi-Agent Demonstrations

author.name: Lasse Peters, Laura Ferranti, Javier Alonso-Mora, Andrea Bajcsy

entry.summary: Presents Coordinated Diffusion (CoDi), a framework that couples independently trained single-agent diffusion policies through a multi-agent cost function to generate coordinated multi-agent behavior without requiring any multi-agent demonstrations. Addresses the exponential data bottleneck in multi-agent imitation learning.

entry.title: Hindsight Hint Distillation: Scaffolded Reasoning for SWE Agents from CoT-free Answers

author.name: Shengjie Wang, Guanghe Li, Zonghan Yang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes Hindsight Hint Distillation (HHD), which generates hints from a model's own failed rollouts to scaffold successful trajectories, then self-distills these without requiring explicit chain-of-thought annotations. Only needs question-answer pairs.

entry.title: SoK: Unlearnability and Unlearning for Model Dememorization

author.name: Mengying Zhang, Derui Wang, Ruoxi Sun, Xiaoyu Xia, Shuang Hao, Minhui Xue

entry.summary: Provides a systematization of knowledge (SoK) connecting unlearnability (training-stage) and machine unlearning (post-training) as complementary model dememorization methods, analyzing their shared vulnerabilities.

entry.title: TMRL: Diffusion Timestep-Modulated Pretraining Enables Exploration for Efficient Policy Finetuning

author.name: Matthew M. Hong, Jesse Zhang, Anusha Nagabandi, Abhishek Gupta

entry.summary: Presents TMRL, a framework bridging BC pre-training and RL fine-tuning for robot policies by injecting forward-diffusion noise during pre-training (Context-Smoothed Pre-training) and adaptively adjusting noise during RL fine-tuning.

entry.title: Unlearning with Asymmetric Sources: Improved Unlearning-Utility Trade-off with Public Data

author.name: Ahmed Mehdi Inane, Vincent Quirion, Gintare Karolina Dzugaite, Ioannis Mitliagkas

entry.summary: Introduces Asymmetric Langevin Unlearning (ALU) showing that public data injection suppresses unlearning noise cost by O(1/n_pub²), providing a strict computational advantage over retraining for certified unlearning.

entry.title: Adaptive Teacher Exposure for Self-Distillation in LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zihao Han, Tiangang Zhang, Huaibin Wang, Yilun Sun

entry.summary: Identifies 'teacher-side exposure mismatch' in on-policy self-distillation for LLM reasoning: when the teacher sees the full reference beyond the student's competence, targets become too strong. Proposes adaptive teacher exposure that adjusts conditioning based on student capability.

entry.title: A Study on Hidden Layer Distillation for Large Language Model Pre-Training

author.name: Maxime Guigon, Lucas Dixon, Micha\"el E. Sander

entry.summary: Studies hidden layer distillation for LLM pre-training using Gemma3 3.4B as teacher. Finds that hidden layer distillation doesn't consistently outperform standard KD on downstream tasks but provides insights on when it helps.

entry.title: Premover: Fast Vision-Language-Action Control by Acting Before Instructions Are Complete

author.name: Joonha Park, Jiseung Jeong, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: Introduces Premover, a module that starts precomputing VLA policy outputs while the user is still typing instructions, using projected image-language focus maps to identify likely target objects before the full instruction is received.

entry.title: Neural Statistical Functions

author.name: Daniel Xu, Yuxin Xie, Minghao Guo, Haixu Wu, Wojciech Matusik

entry.summary: Neural statistical functions learn to directly predict statistical quantities (integrals, quantiles, maxima) over continuous operating conditions from pre-trained predictors, avoiding repeated inference through a unified interval-conditional framework.

entry.title: From Web to Pixels: Bringing Agentic Search into Visual Perception

author.name: Bokang Yang, Xinyi Sun, Kaituo Feng, Xingping Dong, Dongming Wu, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: WebEye formalizes 'Perception Deep Research' where visible objects must be resolved through external knowledge search before localization. Benchmark combines search-based grounding, segmentation, and VQA with verifiable evidence chains.

entry.title: EVOCHAMBER: Test-Time Co-evolution of Multi-Agent System at Individual, Team, and Population Scales

author.name: Yaolun Zhang, Tianyi Xu, Shengyu Dai, Zhenwen Shao, Qingyun Wu, Huazheng Wang

entry.summary: Presents EVOCHAMBER, a training-free framework for test-time evolution of multi-agent systems at three scales: individual, team, and population. The key insight is that multi-agent evolution requires mechanisms for evolving collaboration structures and knowledge flow, not just replicating single-agent evolution.

entry.title: Rethinking Evaluation for LLM Hallucination Detection: A Desiderata, A New RAG-based Benchmark, New Insights

author.name: Wenbo Chen, Veena Padmanabhan, Tootiya Giyahchi, Elaine Wong, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: Establishes a desiderata for hallucination detection benchmarks and reveals that no existing benchmark satisfies all properties. Identifies two major gaps: RAG-based benchmarks with long context and difficulty-stratified evaluation, then provides a new benchmark addressing these.

entry.title: Causal Bias Detection in Generative Artifical Intelligence

author.name: Drago Plecko

entry.summary: Extends causal fairness frameworks from standard ML to generative AI, where models construct multiple causal mechanisms simultaneously. Provides principled causal inference approaches for detecting bias in generative systems.

entry.title: FibQuant: Universal Vector Quantization for Random-Access KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Namyoon Lee, Yongjune Kim

entry.summary: Introduces FibQuant, a universal fixed-rate vector quantizer for KV-cache compression that exploits the spherical-Beta geometry created by normalization in rotation-based codecs. Replaces scalar tables with lattice codebooks on the unit ball.

entry.title: Nice Fold or Hero Call: Learning Budget-Efficient Thinking for Adaptive Reasoning

author.name: Zhaomeng Zhou, Lan Zhang, Junyang Wang, Mu Yuan, Junda Lin

entry.summary: Proposes Budget-Efficient Thinking (BET) that formulates adaptive reasoning as computational investment under uncertainty, allocating budget based on expected return rather than perceived difficulty alone. Accounts for query solvability to avoid wasting compute on impossible problems.

entry.title: When Simulation Lies: A Sim-to-Real Benchmark and Domain-Randomized RL Recipe for Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Xiaolin Zhou, Aojie Yuan, Zheng Luo, Zipeng Ling, Xixiao Pan, Yicheng Gao, Haiyue Zhang, Jiate Li, Shuli Jiang, Prince Zizhuang Wang, Zixuan Zhu, Jinbo Liu, Ryan A. Rossi, Hua Wei, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: Introduces RobustBench-TC, a benchmark with 22 perturbation types for tool-use language agents, grounded in real GitHub issues. Studies the sim-to-real gap where benchmarks assume clean inputs but deployment has typos, timeouts, and duplicate tools.

entry.title: SAGE: A Self-Evolving Agentic Graph-Memory Engine for Structure-Aware Associative Memory

author.name: Juntong Wang, Haoyue Zhao, guanghui Pan, Xiyuan Wang, Yanbo Wang, Qiyan Deng, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SAGE, a self-evolving agentic graph-memory engine that models memory as a dynamic substrate with a writer for constructing structured graph memory and a Graph Foundation Model-based reader for retrieval. Addresses limitations of static RAG/GraphRAG systems.

entry.title: Semantic Reward Collapse and the Preservation of Epistemic Integrity in Adaptive AI Systems

author.name: William Parris

entry.summary: Proposes 'Semantic Reward Collapse' (SRC) - the compression of semantically distinct forms of dissatisfaction (factual errors, uncertainty, formatting, latency) into generalized optimization signals in RLHF, explaining behaviors like sycophancy and hallucinated certainty.

entry.title: Steering Without Breaking: Mechanistically Informed Interventions for Discrete Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Hanhan Zhou, Shamik Roy, Rashmi Gangadharaiah

entry.summary: Shows that uniform intervention schedules degrade quality in discrete diffusion language models and reveals through sparse autoencoders that different attributes commit on distinct schedules. Proposes mechanistically-informed non-uniform steering.

entry.title: The Authorization-Execution Gap Is a Major Safety and Security Problem in Open-World Agents

author.name: Baoyuan Wu, Qingshan Liu, Adel Bibi, Irwin King, Siwei Lyu

entry.summary: Position paper arguing the Authorization-Execution Gap (AEG) is a major safety problem in open-world agents, identifying three structural sources: delegation-level incompleteness, channel-level corruption, and composition-level fragmentation.

entry.title: DisagMoE: Computation-Communication overlapped MoE Training via Disaggregated AF-Pipe Parallelism

author.name: Zhichen Zeng, Chi-Chih Chang, Jiayi Wang, Zezhou Wang, Ningxin Zheng, Zheng Zhong, Cesar A. Stuardo, Dongyang Wang, Mohamed S. Abdelfattah, Haibin Lin, Banghua Zhu, Ang Li, Ziheng Jiang

entry.summary: Presents DisagMoE, a disaggregated MoE training system that jointly optimizes model placement and scheduling to overlap all-to-all communication with computation, addressing bandwidth bottlenecks in trillion-parameter model training.

entry.title: Trust Region Inverse Reinforcement Learning: Explicit Dual Ascent using Local Policy Updates

author.name: Anish Diwan, Davide Tateo, Christopher E. Mower, Haitham Bou-Ammar, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

entry.summary: Bridges classical dual-ascent IRL and modern adversarial approaches by enabling monotonic improvement of both reward and policy without fully solving an RL problem each iteration. Uses trust-region constraints for theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: On Problems of Implicit Context Compression for Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Kirill Gelvan, Igor Slinko, Felix Steinbauer, Egor Bogomolov, Florian Kofler, Yaroslav Zharov

entry.summary: Investigates why continuous embedding-based context compression (In-Context Autoencoder) works for single-shot tasks but fails for multi-step agentic coding tasks. Explores factors contributing to this failure mode.

entry.title: MCPShield: Content-Aware Attack Detection for LLM Agent Tool-Call Traffic

author.name: Sultan Zavrak

entry.summary: MCPShield detects attacks on MCP tool-call traffic by encoding agent sessions as graphs and classifying them with GNNs. Evaluates GAT, GCN, GraphSAGE and baselines on tool-call traces.

entry.title: Birds of a Feather Flock Together: Background-Invariant Representations via Linear Structure in VLMs

author.name: Youssef Zaazou, Mark Thomas

entry.summary: Shows that linear additivity in VLM embedding spaces enables decomposition into foreground/background components. Uses this to construct background-invariant representations via synthetic data pre-training.

entry.title: ReCoVer: Resilient LLM Pre-Training System via Fault-Tolerant Collective and Versatile Workload

author.name: Ziyue Liu, Zhengyang Wang, Ruijie Zhang, Avinash Maurya, Hui Zhou, Paul Hovland, Sheng Di, Franck Cappello, Bogdan Nicolae, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: ReCoVer provides fault-tolerant LLM pre-training by maintaining constant microbatch count per iteration to ensure stochastic equivalence with failure-free runs. Implements fault-tolerant collectives and fine-grained recovery.

entry.title: gwBenchmarks: Stress-Testing LLM Agents on High-Precision Gravitational Wave Astronomy

author.name: Tousif Islam, Digvijay Wadekar, Zihan Zhou

entry.summary: gwBenchmarks stress-tests LLM coding agents on gravitational wave astronomy tasks requiring extreme precision (10^-4 relative error). Eight tasks spanning waveform surrogates, orbital dynamics, and template banks.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity: Temporal Operator Attention for Time Series Analysis

author.name: Jevon Twitty, Vinh Pham, Nitiwith Rotchanarak, Viresh Pati, Yubin Kim, Shihao Yang, Jiecheng Lu

entry.summary: Proposes Temporal Operator Attention (TOA) that replaces softmax attention's simplex-constrained mixing with unconstrained operator learning for time series. Formalizes the limitation as a simplex bottleneck.

entry.title: Natural Language based Specification and Verification

author.name: Zhaorui Li, Chengyu Song

entry.summary: Investigates using LLMs for both specification generation and compositional verification when specs are in natural language rather than formal notation. Aims to prevent LLM-generated vulnerable code.

entry.title: Predictive Maps of Multi-Agent Reasoning: A Successor-Representation Spectrum for LLM Communication Topologies

author.name: Ethan David James Park, Dalal Alharthi

entry.summary: Introduces a spectral diagnostic framework for multi-agent LLM communication topologies using successor representations. Connects spectral quantities to drift, convergence, and robustness properties of agent communication graphs.

entry.title: Decaf: Improving Neural Decompilation with Automatic Feedback and Search

author.name: Alexander Shypula, Osbert Bastani, Edward Schwartz

entry.summary: Proposes Decaf, which improves neural decompilation by using compiler feedback and search rather than simply scaling data/training. Uses compiler verification as automatic feedback for iterative improvement.

entry.title: When Emotion Becomes Trigger: Emotion-style dynamic Backdoor Attack Parasitising Large Language Models

author.name: Ziyu Liu, Tao Li, Tianjie Ni, Xiaolong Lan, Wengang Ma, Tao Yang, Guohua Wang, Junjiang He

entry.summary: Proposes emotion-style dynamic backdoor attacks on LLMs using emotional tone as a trigger rather than fixed tokens. Shows emotion can be decoupled from semantics in LLM representation space.

entry.title: Minimax Rates and Spectral Distillation for Tree Ensembles

author.name: Binh Duc Vu, David S. Watson

entry.summary: Derives minimax-optimal convergence rates for random forest regression via spectral analysis of the induced kernel operator, and develops spectral compression schemes for tree ensembles.

entry.title: Incentivizing Truthfulness and Collaborative Fairness in Bayesian Learning

author.name: Rachael Hwee Ling Sim, Jue Fan, Xiao Tian, Xinyi Xu, Patrick Jaillet, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low

entry.summary: Presents the first mechanism that provably ensures collaborative fairness and incentivizes truthful data sharing in Bayesian collaborative machine learning, combining semivalues with truthful data verification.

entry.title: Scaling Laws and Tradeoffs in Recurrent Networks of Expressive Neurons

author.name: Aaron Spieler, Georg Martius, Anna Levina

entry.summary: Investigates how to optimally allocate a fixed parameter budget between number of units, per-unit complexity, and connectivity in recurrent networks. Introduces ELM Networks with tunable per-unit complexity and derives scaling laws.

entry.title: It's Not the Size: Harness Design Determines Operational Stability in Small Language Models

author.name: Yong-eun Cho

entry.summary: Experimentally shows that a 4-stage pipeline harness (plan→execute→verify→recover) dramatically improves small language model performance, achieving near-perfect task success on 2-3B models. Identifies 'scaffold collapse' where minimal wrappers hurt performance.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Laplace Approximation for Bayesian Uncertainty Quantification

author.name: Julian Rodemann, Alexander Marquard, Thomas Augustin, Michele Caprio

entry.summary: Proposes self-supervised Laplace approximation that bypasses parameter posteriors to directly approximate predictive uncertainty by refitting on self-predicted data. High likelihood on self-predictions indicates low uncertainty.

entry.title: Fill the GAP: A Granular Alignment Paradigm for Visual Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yanting Miao, Yutao Sun, Dexin Wang, Mengyu Zhou, Pascal Poupart, Lei Lv, Qi Zhao, Li Wang, Hao Li, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes Fill the GAP for visual latent reasoning in MLLMs, identifying a feature-space norm mismatch between decoder hidden states and input embeddings that makes direct latent feedback unreliable.

entry.title: KV-Fold: One-Step KV-Cache Recurrence for Long-Context Inference

author.name: Alireza Nadali, Patrick Cooper, Ashutosh Trivedi, Alvaro Velasquez

entry.summary: Introduces KV-Fold, a training-free protocol that processes long contexts by treating the KV cache as an accumulator in a left fold over sequence chunks, enabling long-context inference without architectural changes.

entry.title: AlphaGRPO: Unlocking Self-Reflective Multimodal Generation in UMMs via Decompositional Verifiable Reward

author.name: Runhui Huang, Jie Wu, Rui Yang, Zhe Liu, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes AlphaGRPO, applying GRPO to AR-Diffusion Unified Multimodal Models with Decompositional Verifiable Rewards, enabling self-reflective reasoning in text-to-image generation without cold-start.

entry.title: GRAFT-ATHENA: Self-Improving Agentic Teams for Autonomous Discovery and Evolutionary Numerical Algorithms

author.name: Juan Diego Toscano, Zhaojie Chai, George Em Karniadakis

entry.summary: Introduces GRAFT-ATHENA, a self-improving agentic framework that learns from past scientific problems and autonomously expands its action space across domains using graph-based representations of methodological choices.

entry.title: Latent Chain-of-Thought Improves Structured-Data Transformers

author.name: Carson Dudley, Samet Oymak

entry.summary: Explores latent chain-of-thought for structured-data transformers (time-series, tabular), using a recurrent scheme where hidden states are compressed into feedback tokens and reprocessed for multiple rounds of computation before prediction.

entry.title: Optimal Representations for Generalized Contrastive Learning with Imbalanced Datasets

author.name: Thuan Nguyen, Shuchin Aeron, D. Richard Brown III, Prakash Ishwar

entry.summary: Characterizes optimal representation geometry in contrastive learning with imbalanced classes, proving that class means exhibit angular symmetry determined by class proportions rather than the ETF structure seen in balanced settings.

entry.title: VERDI: Single-Call Confidence Estimation for Verification-Based LLM Judges via Decomposed Inference

author.name: Jasmine Qi, Danylo Dantsev, Muyang Sun

entry.summary: VERDI extracts confidence estimates from verification-based LLM judges by decomposing reasoning traces into sub-checks and deriving structural signals, requiring no additional inference calls.

entry.title: Efficient Adjoint Matching for Fine-tuning Diffusion Models

author.name: Jeongwoo Shin, Dongsoo Shin, Joonseok Lee, Jaewoong Choi, Jaemoo Choi

entry.summary: Improves Adjoint Matching for diffusion model fine-tuning by eliminating computational bottlenecks tied to non-trivial base drift, reducing function evaluations for trajectory simulation and backward ODE computation.

entry.title: Adaptive Calibration in Non-Stationary Environments

author.name: Junyan Liu, Haipeng Luo, Lillian J. Ratliff

entry.summary: Develops adaptive calibration algorithms that automatically adjust to the degree of non-stationarity, interpolating between i.i.d. and adversarial regimes with sublinear calibration error bounds.

entry.title: Gradient Clipping Beyond Vector Norms: A Spectral Approach for Matrix-Valued Parameters

author.name: Alexander Yukhimchuk, Mladen Kolar, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Sayantan Choudhury

entry.summary: Proposes spectral gradient clipping that clamps individual singular values exceeding a threshold while preserving singular directions, motivated by the observation that outliers amplify only leading singular values.

entry.title: Expected Batch Optimal Transport Plans and Consequences for Flow Matching

author.name: Samuel Bo\"it\'e, Julie Delon, Kimia Nadjahi

entry.summary: Formalizes the population-level coupling induced by minibatch optimal transport in flow matching as 'expected batch OT plan', proves large-batch consistency, and derives convergence rates. Shows that for generative modeling, batch OT actually yields straighter flows than global OT.

entry.title: Autoregressive Learning in Joint KL: Sharp Oracle Bounds and Lower Bounds

author.name: Yunbei Xu, Yuzhe Yuan, Ruohan Zhan

entry.summary: Provides the first complete characterization of how sequence horizon H affects approximation and estimation errors in autoregressive modeling under model misspecification, measured by joint KL divergence. Shows joint KL admits horizon-free approximation, contrasting with Hellinger distance.

entry.title: Pion: A Spectrum-Preserving Optimizer via Orthogonal Equivalence Transformation

author.name: Kexuan Shi, Hanxuan Li, Zeju Qiu, Yandong Wen, Simon Buchholz, Weiyang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Pion, an optimizer for LLM training that updates weight matrices through orthogonal transformations, preserving singular values throughout training. Modulates weight geometry while keeping spectral norm fixed, offering a fundamentally different optimization mechanism from additive optimizers like Adam/Muon.

entry.title: Attacks and Mitigations for Distributed Governance of Agentic AI under Byzantine Adversaries

author.name: Matthew D. Laws, Alina Oprea, Cristina Nita-Rotaru

entry.summary: Analyzes security vulnerabilities in distributed governance of agentic AI systems, specifically addressing Byzantine adversaries targeting the centralized Provider in SAGA. Proposes distributed governance protocols resilient to compromised trust points.

entry.title: Elastic Attention Cores for Scalable Vision Transformers

author.name: Alan Z. Song, Yinjie Chen, Mu Nan, Rui Zhang, Jiahang Cao, Weijian Mai, Muquan Yu, Hossein Adeli, Deva Ramanan, Michael J. Tarr, Andrew F. Luo

entry.summary: Proposes VECA, a Vision Transformer that replaces all-to-all self-attention with linear-time core-periphery structured attention using learned cores. Demonstrates effective visual representations can be learned without direct patch-to-patch interaction.

entry.title: BitLM: Unlocking Multi-Token Language Generation with Bitwise Continuous Diffusion

author.name: Shaobin Zhuang, Yuang Ai, Jiaming Han, Xiaohui Li, Huaibo Huang, Xiangyu Yue, Xuefeng Hu, Kun Xu, Yali Wang, Hao Chen

entry.summary: Proposes BitLM, a language model that represents tokens as binary codes and uses a lightweight diffusion head to denoise multiple tokens in parallel while preserving left-to-right causal structure. Addresses the one-token generation bottleneck.

entry.title: PRISM: Pareto-Efficient Retrieval over Intent-Aware Structured Memory for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Jingyi Peng, Zhongwei Wan, Weiting Liu, Qiuzhuang Sun

entry.summary: Presents PRISM, a training-free framework for managing long-horizon agent memory using graph-structured retrieval with hierarchical bundle search and query-sensitive edge costing for Pareto-efficient accuracy-cost tradeoffs.

entry.title: GKnow: Measuring the Entanglement of Gender Bias and Factual Gender

author.name: Leonor Veloso, Hinrich Sch\"utze

entry.summary: Introduces GKnow, a benchmark to disentangle factual gender knowledge from gender bias in language models, enabling analysis of circuits responsible for each. Addresses the critical distinction between correct gendered outputs and stereotyped ones.

entry.title: CheXTemporal: A Dataset for Temporally-Grounded Reasoning in Chest Radiography

author.name: Eva Prakash, Yunhe Gao, Chong Wang, Justin Xu, Neal Prakash, Arne Michalson, Seena Dehkharghani, Eun Kyoung Hong, Julie Bauml, Roger Boodoo, Jean-Benoit Delbrouck, Sophie Ostmeier, Curtis Langlotz

entry.summary: Introduces CheXTemporal, a dataset for temporally-grounded reasoning in chest radiography with finding-level progression annotations (new/worse/stable/improved/resolved) and spatial-temporal alignment across prior-current study pairs.

entry.title: Principled Design of Diffusion-based Optimizers for Inverse Problems

author.name: Julio Oscanoa, Irmak Sivgin, Cagan Alkan, Daniel Ennis, John Pauly, Mert Pilanci, Shreyas Vasanawala

entry.summary: Proposes principled reparameterizations for diffusion-based inverse problem solvers that enable hyperparameter reuse across problems, plus OptDiff pipeline combining optimization with denoising for faster convergence.

entry.title: Dynamic Execution Commitment of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Feng Chen, Xianghui Wang, Yuxuan Chen, Boying Li, Yefei He, Zeyu Zhang, Yicheng Wu

entry.summary: Introduces A3 (Adaptive Action Acceptance), a mechanism for Vision-Language-Action models that dynamically decides how many steps of a predicted action chunk to commit to, based on state-dependent predictive reliability.

entry.title: Logit-Attention Divergence: Mitigating Position Bias in Multi-Image Retrieval via Attention-Guided Calibration

author.name: Mingtao Xian, Yifeng Yang, Qinying Gu, Xinbing Wang, Nanyang Ye

entry.summary: Identifies Logit-Attention Divergence in MLLMs where output logits show position bias but internal attention maps remain correctly aligned. Proposes training-free attention-guided debiasing for multi-image retrieval.

entry.title: RNA-FM: Flow-Matching Generative Model for Genome-wide RNA-Seq Prediction

author.name: Yaxuan Song, Jianan Fan, Tianyi Wang, Qiuyue Hu, Hang Chang, Heng Huang, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: Proposes RNA-FM, a flow-matching generative framework for predicting genome-wide RNA-seq expression from histopathology whole-slide images, capturing biological heterogeneity through generative modeling.

entry.title: Learn to Think: Improving Multimodal Reasoning through Vision-Aware Self-Improvement Training

author.name: Qihuang Zhong, Liang Ding, Wenjie Xuan, Juhua Liu, Bo Du, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: VISTA addresses two shortcomings of self-improvement training for multimodal reasoning: data imbalance (overtraining simple samples) and language prior bias (over-reliance on text, neglecting visual cues). Proposes vision-aware self-improvement training.

entry.title: What-Where Transformer: A Slot-Centric Visual Backbone for Concurrent Representation and Localization

author.name: Ryota Yoshihashi, Masahiro Kada, Satoshi Ikehata, Rei Kawakami, Ikuro Sato

entry.summary: What-Where Transformer proposes slot-centric visual backbone that decomposes object appearance (what) and spatial location (where) in a ViT-style architecture. Addresses the limitation that classification-oriented backbones suppress spatial information.

entry.title: Beyond Text Prompts: Visual-to-Visual Generation as A Unified Paradigm

author.name: Yaofang Liu, Kangning Cui, Meng Chu, Zhaoqing Li, Suiyun Zhang, Jean-Michel Morel, Xiaodong Cun, Haoxuan Che, Rui Liu, Raymond H. Chan

entry.summary: Proposes visual-to-visual (V2V) generation paradigm where users condition generative models with visual specification pages instead of text prompts. V2V-Zero is a training-free framework replacing text conditioning with visual documents.

entry.title: Kairos: A Scalable Serving System for Physical AI

author.name: Yinwei Dai, Ganesh Ananthanarayanan, Landon Cox, Xenofon Foukas, Bozidar Radunovic, Ravi Netravali

entry.summary: Presents Kairos, the first multi-robot serving system designed specifically for Physical AI workloads, which differ from digital AI in their multi-round inference-action execution loops and asynchronous interleaving. Makes the generate-execute loop a first-class abstraction for serving robot fleets at scale.

entry.title: EvoNav: Evolutionary Reward Function Design for Robot Navigation with Large Language Models

author.name: Zhikai Zhao, Chuanbo Hua, Federico Berto, Zihan Ma, Kanghoon Lee, Jiachen Li, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: Proposes EvoNav, an evolutionary framework using LLMs to automatically design reward functions for robot navigation, with progressive evaluation stages to reduce training cost.

entry.title: Emergent Communication between Heterogeneous Visual Agents through Decentralized Learning

author.name: Mikako Ochiai, Masatoshi Nagano, Tadahiro Taniguchi

entry.summary: Studies emergent communication between agents with heterogeneous visual representations through decentralized learning, examining whether common symbols can arise without shared perceptual access.

entry.title: OmniHumanoid: Streaming Cross-Embodiment Video Generation with Paired-Free Adaptation

author.name: Yiren Song, Xiyao Deng, Pei Yang, Yihan Wang, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: OmniHumanoid enables cross-embodiment video generation (human-to-robot, robot-to-robot) by factorizing transferable motion and embodiment-specific appearance. Scales to new robots without paired data through paired-free adaptation.

entry.title: CausalCine: Real-Time Autoregressive Generation for Multi-Shot Video Narratives

author.name: Yihao Meng, Zichen Liu, Hao Ouyang, Qiuyu Wang, Ka Leong Cheng, Yue Yu, Hanlin Wang, Haobo Li, Jiapeng Zhu, Yanhong Zeng, Xing Zhu, Yujun Shen, Qifeng Chen, Huamin Qu

entry.summary: CausalCine is an autoregressive framework for multi-shot video generation that treats cinematic storytelling as an online directing process with dynamic prompts, viewpoint shifts, and shot boundaries.

entry.title: LatentRouter: Can We Choose the Right Multimodal Model Before Seeing Its Answer?

author.name: Xueqi Cheng, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: Proposes LatentRouter, a model routing system for multimodal LLMs that predicts counterfactual utility of each candidate model for a given image-question query. Uses learned multimodal routing capsules and model capability tokens for latent communication.

entry.title: Causal Algorithmic Recourse: Foundations and Methods

author.name: Drago Plecko, Collin Wang, Elias Bareinboim

entry.summary: Develops a causal framework for algorithmic recourse that models it as a process over pre- and post-intervention outcomes, allowing for partial stability and resampling of latent variables. Introduces post-recourse stability conditions enabling reasoning from observational data alone.

entry.title: Selective Off-Policy Reference Tuning with Plan Guidance

author.name: Duc Anh Le, Tien-Phat Nguyen, Thien Huu Nguyen, Linh Ngo Van, Trung Le

entry.summary: Proposes SORT, which adds repair updates for prompts where all GRPO rollouts fail by deriving plans from reference solutions and selectively weighting tokens that become more predictable under plan conditioning. Turns all-wrong prompts into selective learning signals.

entry.title: AutoLLMResearch: Training Research Agents for Automating LLM Experiment Configuration -- Learning from Cheap, Optimizing Expensive

author.name: Taicheng Guo, Nitesh V. Chawla, Olaf Wiest, Xiangliang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AutoLLMResearch, an agentic framework that automates expensive LLM experiment configuration (architecture, hyperparameters) by learning from cheap proxy experiments to optimize expensive ones. Mimics human researcher intuition transfer.

entry.title: Toward Stable Value Alignment: Introducing Independent Modules for Consistent Value Guidance

author.name: Wenhao Chen, Sirui Sun, Shengyuan Bai, Guojie Song

entry.summary: Proposes Stable Value Guidance Transformer (SVGT), which maintains normative representations in an independent value module isolated from the backbone's dynamic residual stream. Addresses instability of value expression in standard RLHF-aligned models.

entry.title: MedMemoryBench: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Personalized Healthcare

author.name: Yihao Wang, Haoran Xu, Renjie Gu, Yixuan Ye, Xinyi Chen, Xinyu Mu, Yuan Gao, Chunxiao Guo, Peng Wei, Jinjie Gu, Huan Li, Ke Chen, Lidan Shou

entry.summary: Introduces MedMemoryBench, a benchmark for evaluating agent memory in personalized healthcare with ~10K realistic long-horizon medical trajectories. Developed through human-agent collaboration based on clinically grounded patient archetypes.

entry.title: Assessing and Mitigating Miscalibration in LLM-Based Social Science Measurement

author.name: Jinyuan Wang, Ningyuan Deng, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Studies miscalibration in LLM-based social science measurement across 14 constructs and shows that confidence-based filtering can change downstream regression estimates. Audits calibration of proprietary models including GPT-5-mini and DeepSeek-V3.

entry.title: BadSKP: Backdoor Attacks on Knowledge Graph-Enhanced LLMs with Soft Prompts

author.name: Xiaoting Lyu, Yufei Han, Hangwei Qian, Haoyuan Yu, Xiang Ao, Bin Wang, Chenxu Wang, Xiaobo Ma, Wei Wang

entry.summary: Demonstrates a robustness gap in knowledge graph-enhanced LLMs where text-channel backdoor attacks fail against soft-prompt-based graph encoding, then proposes a new dual-channel backdoor attack (BadSKP) that exploits this architecture. Introduces concept of 'semantic anchoring' by graph-derived soft prompts.

entry.title: $\delta$-mem: Efficient Online Memory for Large Language Models

author.name: Jingdi Lei, Di Zhang, Junxian Li, Weida Wang, Kaixuan Fan, Xiang Liu, Qihan Liu, Xiaoteng Ma, Baian Chen, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: Proposes δ-mem, a lightweight memory mechanism augmenting frozen LLMs with a compact 8×8 online state matrix updated by delta-rule learning. Provides low-rank corrections to backbone attention during generation, achieving 1.10x improvement over frozen backbone.

entry.title: Formalize, Don't Optimize: The Heuristic Trap in LLM-Generated Combinatorial Solvers

author.name: Haoyu Wang, Yuliang Song, Tao Li, Zhiwei Deng, Yaqing Wang, Deepak Ramachandran, Eldan Cohen, Dan Roth

entry.summary: Introduces CP-SynC-XL benchmark (100 problems, 4,577 instances) and evaluates three solver-construction paradigms for LLMs. Finds Python+OR-Tools achieves highest correctness while native Python heuristics show worst scaling despite LLMs preferring to write them.

entry.title: MT-JailBench: A Modular Benchmark for Understanding Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Xinkai Zhang, Zhipeng Wei, Huanli Gong, Jing Ting Zheng, Yuchen Zhang, Yue Dong, N. Benjamin Erichson

entry.summary: Introduces MT-JailBench, a modular evaluation framework for multi-turn jailbreak attacks with five interacting modules, enabling fair comparison under fixed conditions. Addresses confounding factors in existing multi-turn attack evaluations.

entry.title: ForceFlow: Learning to Feel and Act via Contact-Driven Flow Matching

author.name: Shuoheng Zhang, Yifu Yuan, Hongyao Tang, Yan Zheng, Qiaojun Yu, Pengyi Li, Guowei Huang, Helong Huang, Xingyue Quan, Jianye Hao

entry.summary: ForceFlow integrates force/torque sensing into imitation learning via flow matching for contact-rich manipulation. Uses asymmetric multimodal fusion treating force as a global conditioning signal.

entry.title: HEPA: A Self-Supervised Horizon-Conditioned Event Predictive Architecture for Time Series

author.name: Jonas Petersen (ETH Zurich, Forgis), Gian-Alessandro Lombardi (Forgis), Riccardo Maggioni (Forgis), Camilla Mazzoleni (Forgis), Federico Martelli (ETH Zurich, Forgis), Philipp Petersen (University of Vienna)

entry.summary: HEPA uses a JEPA-based self-supervised approach for time series event prediction with horizon conditioning. Pretrained encoder captures temporal dynamics, then predictor is finetuned to produce survival CDFs.

entry.title: ClinicalBench: Stress-Testing Assertion-Aware Retrieval for Cross-Admission Clinical QA on MIMIC-IV

author.name: Alex Stinard

entry.summary: ClinicalBench evaluates retrieval over real EHR notes where negation, temporality, and attribution can flip answers. Tests assertion-aware retrieval (EpiKG) across six LLMs on 400 MIMIC-IV questions.

entry.title: ABRA: Agent Benchmark for Radiology Applications

author.name: Bulat Maksudov, Vladislav Kurenkov, Kathleen M. Curran, Alessandra Mileo

entry.summary: ABRA benchmarks radiology agents that must operate OHIF viewer and DICOM server through 21 tools. Includes 655 tasks across three difficulty tiers spanning viewer control, annotation, and reporting.

entry.title: Curriculum Learning-Guided Progressive Distillation in Large Language Models

author.name: Jincheng Cao, Fanzhi Zeng, Leqi Liu, Aryan Mokhtari

entry.summary: CLPD proposes curriculum learning-guided progressive distillation that aligns data difficulty with teacher strength, addressing the counter-intuitive phenomenon where stronger teachers produce worse students.

entry.title: SOMA: Efficient Multi-turn LLM Serving via Small Language Model

author.name: Xueqi Cheng, Qiong Wu, Zhengyi Zhou, Xugui Zhou, Tyler Derr, Yushun Dong

entry.summary: SOMA reduces multi-turn LLM serving costs by using early turns to estimate a local response manifold, then adapting a smaller surrogate model with soft prompts for remaining conversation turns.

entry.title: MaskTab: Scalable Masked Tabular Pretraining with Scaling Laws and Distillation for Industrial Classification

author.name: Bo Zheng, Yudong Chen, Zihua Xiong, Shuai Fang, Peidong He, Yang Yang, Sheng Guo

entry.summary: MaskTab provides masked tabular pre-training at industrial scale with dedicated missing-value tokens, twin-path architecture, and scaling laws for tabular foundation models with distillation.

entry.title: Efficient and provably convergent end-to-end training of deep neural networks with linear constraints

author.name: Zonglin Yang, Zhexuan Gu, Yancheng Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces an efficient end-to-end training framework for deep neural networks with linear constraints on selected layers. Develops HS-Jacobian for handling nonsmoothness of projection layers with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: TCP-SSM: Efficient Vision State Space Models with Token-Conditioned Poles

author.name: Sara Shoouri, Morteza Tavakoli Taba, Hun-Seok Kim

entry.summary: Proposes TCP-SSM, a state space model with token-conditioned poles that makes recurrence dynamics explicit and interpretable. Targets efficient vision backbones with controllable state-dependent memory.

entry.title: Shaping Zero-Shot Coordination via State Blocking

author.name: Mingu Kang, Sunwoo Lee, Yonghyeon Jo, Seungyul Han

entry.summary: Introduces State-Blocked Coordination (SBC) for zero-shot coordination in multi-agent systems. Creates virtual environments through state blocking to expose agents to diverse suboptimal partner policies.

entry.title: CaC: Advancing Video Reward Models via Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Concentrating

author.name: Jiyuan Wang, Huan Ouyang, Jiuzhou Lin, Chunyu Lin, Dewen Fan, Boheng Zhang, Haonan Fan, Fei Zuo, Jia Sun, Huaiqing Wang, Honglie Wang, Yiyang Fan, Zhenlong Yuan, Zijun Li, Yongrui Heng, Guosheng Lin, Fan Yang, Tingting Gao

entry.summary: Proposes CaC (Concentrate and Concentrate), a coarse-to-fine video anomaly reward model that uses temporal scanning, spatial grounding, and Chain-of-Thought reasoning for generated video evaluation.

entry.title: OTT-Vid: Optimal Transport Temporal Token Compression for Video Large Language Models

author.name: Minseok Kang, Minhyeok Lee, Jungho Lee, Minjung Kim, Donghyeong Kim, Dayeon Lee, Heeseung Choi, Ig-jae Kim, Sangyoun Lee

entry.summary: Proposes OTT-Vid, using optimal transport for temporal token compression in Video LLMs. Adapts compression strength per frame pair based on semantic content and compressibility.

entry.title: Disentangled Sparse Representations for Concept-Separated Diffusion Unlearning

author.name: Hyeonjin Kim, Hangyeol Jung, Heechan Yun, Sungjun Yun, Dong-Jun Han

entry.summary: Proposes SAEParate for diffusion model unlearning that organizes sparse autoencoder latents into concept-specific clusters via contrastive objectives, enabling more precise concept suppression without modifying model parameters.

entry.title: Mitigating Context-Memory Conflicts in LLMs through Dynamic Cognitive Reconciliation Decoding

author.name: Yigeng Zhou, Wu Li, Yifan Lu, Yequan Wang, Xuebo Liu, Wenya Wang, Jun Yu, Min Zhang, Jing Li

entry.summary: Proposes DCRD, a two-stage decoding method that uses attention maps to detect context-memory conflicts in LLMs, then applies targeted contrastive decoding only when conflicts are predicted, avoiding disruption in conflict-free scenarios.

entry.title: PriorZero: Bridging Language Priors and World Models for Decision Making

author.name: Junyu Xiong, Yuan Pu, Jia Tang, Yazhe Niu

entry.summary: Proposes PriorZero, integrating LLM world knowledge into world-model-based planning through decoupled rollout-training design, addressing the prior-dynamics mismatch between static LLM priors and complex environment dynamics.

entry.title: MedHopQA: A Disease-Centered Multi-Hop Reasoning Benchmark and Evaluation Framework for LLM-Based Biomedical Question Answering

author.name: Rezarta Islamaj, Robert Leaman, Joey Chan, Nicholas Wan, Qiao Jin, Natalie Xie, John Wilbur, Shubo Tian, Lana Yeganova, Po-Ting Lai, Chih-Hsuan Wei, Yifan Yang, Yao Ge, Qingqing Zhu, Zhizheng Wang, Zhiyong Lu

entry.summary: Introduces MedHopQA, a multi-hop reasoning benchmark for biomedical QA that requires integrating information across multiple sources, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks vulnerable to pattern matching and data contamination.

entry.title: OGLS-SD: On-Policy Self-Distillation with Outcome-Guided Logit Steering for LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yuxiao Yang, Xiaoyun Wang, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes OGLS-SD for on-policy self-distillation that uses verifiable outcome rewards to contrast successful/failed trajectories and calibrate teacher logits, addressing reflection-induced bias in teacher responses.

entry.title: Extending Kernel Trick to Influence Functions

author.name: Zhenhuan Sun, Shahrokh Valaee

entry.summary: Presents a dual representation of influence functions whose computational complexity scales with dataset size rather than model size, offering an efficient alternative when models are large relative to datasets.

entry.title: Couple to Control: Joint Initial Noise Design in Diffusion Models

author.name: Jing Jia, Liyue Shen, Guanyang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes joint initial noise design for diffusion models where noise samples are coupled (correlated) while maintaining marginal Gaussian distributions, enabling control over batch diversity and coherence.

entry.title: CTFusion: A CTF-based Benchmark for LLM Agent Evaluation

author.name: Dongjun Lee, Ga-eun Bae, Insu Yun

entry.summary: CTFusion addresses data contamination in LLM cybersecurity agent evaluation by creating a streaming CTF benchmark using live competitions, ensuring per-agent independence and freshness of challenges.

entry.title: GRAFT: Graph-Tokenized LLMs for Tool Planning

author.name: Xinyi Gao, Xinyu Ren, Junliang Yu, Tong Chen, Quoc Viet Hung Nguyen, Hongzhi Yin

entry.summary: GRAFT tokenizes tool dependency graphs and injects them into LLM vocabulary for tool planning, enabling the model to internalize graph constraints during generation rather than relying on external graph retrieval.

entry.title: LOFT: Low-Rank Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Task-Aware Support Selection

author.name: Lanxin Zhao, Bamdev Mishra, Pratik Jawanpuria, Lequan Lin, Dai Shi, Junbin Gao, Andi Han

entry.summary: LOFT unifies orthogonal PEFT methods by separating subspace selection from the orthogonal transformation within that subspace, revealing support selection as the key underexplored design axis.

entry.title: Delightful Gradients Accelerate Corner Escape

author.name: Jincheng Mei, Ian Osband

entry.summary: Introduces 'Delightful Policy Gradient' (DG) that gates policy gradient updates by the product of advantage and action surprisal, proving it escapes sub-optimal corners of the simplex exponentially faster than standard softmax policy gradient. Provides theoretical bounds showing logarithmic escape time vs exponential for standard methods.

entry.title: Grid Games: The Power of Multiple Grids for Quantizing Large Language Models

author.name: Vage Egiazarian, Erik Schultheis, Andrei Panferov, Earl Killian, Torsten Hoefler, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Studies power-of-two-grids (PO2) for 4-bit quantization, where each group can select from multiple grids. Proves theoretically that small-group formats benefit significantly from multiple grids, and instantiates practical grid families including PO2(NF4) that combine multiple quantization grids.

entry.title: Neural-Schwarz Tiling for Geometry-Universal PDE Solving at Scale

author.name: Paolo Secchi, Daniel S. Balint, Marco Maurizi

entry.summary: Introduces NEST (Neural-Schwarz Tiling), a framework that shifts from global neural PDE solvers to reusable local physical solvers that can be composed for arbitrary geometries via domain decomposition (Schwarz method). Enables geometry-universal PDE solving at scale.

entry.title: MEME: Multi-entity & Evolving Memory Evaluation

author.name: Seokwon Jung, Alexander Rubinstein, Arnas Uselis, Sangdoo Yun, Seong Joon Oh

entry.summary: Introduces MEME benchmark for evaluating LLM-based agent memory systems across multi-entity and evolving scenarios, including dependency reasoning tasks. Finds that all tested memory systems collapse on dependency reasoning (Cascade: 3%, Absence: 1% accuracy) despite adequate static retrieval.

entry.title: Posterior Contraction Rates for Sparse Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Anisotropic Besov Spaces

author.name: Jeunghun Oh, Kyeongwon Lee, Jaeyong Lee, Lizhen Lin

entry.summary: Establishes posterior contraction rates for sparse Bayesian Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) over anisotropic Besov spaces, showing near-minimax rates. Demonstrates KANs can achieve these rates with shallower depth than standard MLPs due to built-in compositional structure.

entry.title: Multi-Variable Conformal Prediction: Optimizing Prediction Sets without Data Splitting

author.name: Laura L\"utzow, Simone Garatti, Marco C. Campi, Lars Lindemann, Matthias Althoff

entry.summary: Proposes Multi-variable Conformal Prediction (MCP), extending conformal prediction to vector-valued score functions with multiple calibration variables. Eliminates data splitting by unifying prediction set design and calibration into a single optimization problem using scenario theory.

entry.title: How Does Differential Privacy Affect Social Bias in LLMs? A Systematic Evaluation

author.name: Eduardo Tenorio, Karuna Bhaila, Xintao Wu

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates how differential privacy (DP-SGD) affects social bias in LLMs across four evaluation paradigms. Finds mixed effects: DP reduces bias in sentence scoring but may amplify it in generation tasks.

entry.title: Latent Causal Void: Explicit Missing-Context Reconstruction for Misinformation Detection

author.name: Hui Li, Zhongquan Jian, Jinsong Su, Junfeng Yao

entry.summary: Proposes Latent Causal Void (LCV), a misinformation detector that explicitly reconstructs missing facts that articles omit, using retrieval-guided graph reasoning to identify deceptive omissions.

entry.title: Output Composability of QLoRA PEFT Modules for Plug-and-Play Attribute-Controlled Text Generation

author.name: Michela Lorandi, Anya Belz

entry.summary: Explores composability of QLoRA PEFT modules for controlled text generation, testing training on dataset combinations, weight matrix composition, and output composition across three LLMs and multiple control tasks.

entry.title: Principle-Guided Supervision for Interpretable Uncertainty in Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: An Sui, Yuzhu Li, Gunter Schumann, Fuping Wu, Xiahai Zhuang

entry.summary: Proposes principle-guided uncertainty supervision for medical image segmentation that aligns uncertainty estimates with human-understandable principles: image contrast, corruption severity, and geometric complexity.

entry.title: VidSplat: Gaussian Splatting Reconstruction with Geometry-Guided Video Diffusion Priors

author.name: Jimin Tang, Wenyuan Zhang, Junsheng Zhou, Zian Huang, Kanle Shi, Shenkun Xu, Yu-Shen Liu, Zhizhong Han

entry.summary: Proposes VidSplat, a training-free framework using video diffusion priors to synthesize novel views for sparse-input 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction, compensating for missing input coverage.

entry.title: The DAWN of World-Action Interactive Models

author.name: Hongbo Lu, Liang Yao, Chenghao He, Haoyu Wang, Xiang Gu, Xianfei Li, Wenlong Liao, Tao He, Pai Peng

entry.summary: Proposes DAWN, a World-Action Interactive Model for autonomous driving that couples world prediction with action denoising in a latent space, formalizing the reciprocal dependency between scene evolution and maneuvers.

entry.title: HorizonDrive: Self-Corrective Autoregressive World Model for Long-horizon Driving Simulation

author.name: Conglang Zhang, Yifan Zhan, Qingjie Wang, Zhanpeng Ouyang, Yu Li, Zihao Yang, Xiaoyang Guo, Weiqiang Ren, Qian Zhang, Zhen Dong, Yinqiang Zheng, Wei Yin, Zhengqing Chen

entry.summary: Proposes HorizonDrive, a self-corrective autoregressive world model for long-horizon driving simulation that addresses teacher drift during AR rollout to provide unbounded-horizon supervision.

entry.title: $h$-control: Training-Free Camera Control via Block-Conditional Gibbs Refinement

author.name: Yuzhu Wang, Xi Ye, Duo Su, Yangyang Xu, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: h-control provides training-free camera control for flow-matching video generators through block-conditional Gibbs refinement, treating camera control as a partial-observation inverse problem with provable convergence guarantees.

entry.title: H2G: Hierarchy-Aware Hyperbolic Grouping for 3D Scenes

author.name: ByungHa Ko, Youngmin Lee, Dong Hwan Kim

entry.summary: H2G uses hyperbolic geometry for hierarchical 3D scene grouping, distilling 2D foundation model cues into a Lorentz hyperbolic feature field. The hyperbolic space naturally represents tree-like hierarchical structures.

entry.title: Images in Sentences: Scaling Interleaved Instructions for Unified Visual Generation

author.name: Yabo Zhang, Kunchang Li, Dewei Zhou, Xinyu Huang, Xun Wang

entry.summary: INSET embeds images as native vocabulary within textual instructions for unified visual generation, positioning visual features at their semantic slots to reduce long-range dependencies in interleaved multi-image instructions.

entry.title: See What Matters: Differentiable Grid Sample Pruning for Generalizable Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Yixu Feng, Zinan Zhao, Yanxiang Ma, Chenghao Xia, Chengbin Du, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: GridS is a plug-and-play module for VLA models that performs task-aware continuous visual token resampling, breaking the trade-off between compression rate and preservation of geometric details like contact points.

entry.title: GuidedVLA: Specifying Task-Relevant Factors via Plug-and-Play Action Attention Specialization

author.name: Xiaosong Jia, Bowen Yang, Zuhao Ge, Xian Nie, Yuchen Zhou, Cunxin Fan, Yufeng Li, Yilin Chai, Chao Jing, Zijian Liang, Qingwen Bu, Haidong Cao, Chao Wu, Qifeng Li, Zhenjie Yang, Chenhe Zhang, Hongyang Li, Zuxuan Wu, Junchi Yan, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces GuidedVLA, a framework that manually guides VLA action generation to focus on task-relevant factors by treating attention heads as functional components supervised by manual annotations. Addresses overfitting to spurious correlations in VLA models.

entry.title: OLIVIA: Online Learning via Inference-time Action Adaptation for Decision Making in LLM ReAct Agents

author.name: Sheldon Yu, Junda Wu, Xintong Li, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Sizhe Zhou, Tong Yu, Jiawei Han, Jingbo Shang, Julian McAuley

entry.summary: Introduces OLIVIA, an online learning method for LLM ReAct agents that adapts action selection at inference time using explicit decision layers that can score candidates and be updated from action-level feedback. Addresses the gap between prompting-based adaptation and true online learning for deployed agents.

entry.title: CVEvolve: Autonomous Algorithm Discovery for Unstructured Scientific Data Processing

author.name: Ming Du, Xiangyu Yin, Yanqi Luo, Dishant Beniwal, Songyuan Tang, Hemant Sharma, Mathew J. Cherukara

entry.summary: Introduces CVEvolve, an autonomous agentic system for scientific data-processing algorithm discovery with a zero-code interface. Combines multi-round search with code execution, evaluation, and holdout testing for iterative algorithm improvement.

entry.title: What Do EEG Foundation Models Capture from Human Brain Signals?

author.name: Ling Tang, Qian Chen, Jilin Mei, Houshi Xu, Quanshi Zhang, Jing Shao, Na Zou, Xia Hu, Dongrui Liu

entry.summary: Investigates what EEG foundation models learn by comparing their representations to hand-crafted clinical features using probing, subspace erasure, and transparent classifiers. Addresses whether self-supervised models recapitulate domain knowledge.

entry.title: A CAP-like Trilemma for Large Language Models: Correctness, Non-bias, and Utility under Semantic Underdetermination

author.name: Vinu Ellampallil Venugopal

entry.summary: Formulates a CAP-like trilemma for LLMs: under semantic underdetermination, a model cannot simultaneously guarantee correctness, non-bias, and utility. When premises don't determine a unique answer, useful responses require introducing selection criteria that break non-bias.

entry.title: Beyond World-Frame Action Heads: Motion-Centric Action Frames for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Huoren Yang, Jianchao Zhao, Hu Yusong, Qiguan Ou, Yuyang Gao, Wei Ke, Yuhang He, SongLin Dong, Zhiheng Ma, Yihong Gong

entry.summary: Proposes MCF-Proto, a lightweight action head for VLA models that predicts actions in a learned motion-centric frame rather than fixed world coordinates. Uses prototype-based parameterization with SO(3) rotation prediction.

entry.title: Rethinking Supervision Granularity: Segment-Level Learning for LLM-Based Theorem Proving

author.name: Shuo Xu, Jiakun Zhang, Junyu Lai, Chun Cao, Jingwei Xu

entry.summary: Proposes segment-level supervision for LLM-based theorem proving in Lean 4, finding a middle ground between step-level tactic prediction and whole-proof generation. Extracts locally coherent proof segments as training data and uses same strategy at inference.

entry.title: Missingness-MDPs: Bridging the Theory of Missing Data and POMDPs

author.name: Joshua Wendland, Markel Zubia, Roman Andriushchenko, Maris F. L. Galesloot, Milan Ceska, Henrik von Kleist, Thiago D. Simao, Maximilian Weininger, Nils Jansen

entry.summary: Introduces missingness-MDPs (miss-MDPs), bridging missing data theory with POMDPs. Defines a POMDP subclass whose observation function specifies feature missingness probabilities, and develops planning methods for unknown missingness functions.

entry.title: Context-Gated Associative Retrieval: From Theory to Transformers

author.name: Moulik Choraria, Argyrios Gerogiannis, Vidhata Jayaraman, Ankur Mani, Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage associative memory architecture where a context-gate subcircuit reshapes the retrieval energy landscape, achieving exponential improvements in retrieval. Proves connection to transformer attention mechanisms.

entry.title: Rotation-Preserving Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Hangzhan Jin, Tianwei Ni, Lu Li, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Mohammad Hamdaqa, Doina Precup

entry.summary: Proposes Rotation-Preserving SFT (RPSFT) that penalizes changes in projected top-k singular-vector blocks during fine-tuning, as an efficient proxy for Fisher-sensitive directions. Aims to maintain OOD generalization during domain adaptation.

entry.title: TMPO: Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization for Diverse and Efficient Diffusion Alignment

author.name: Jiaming Li, Chenyu Zhu, Zhiyuan Ma, Nanxi Yi, Youjun Bao, Li Sun, Quanying Lv, Xiang Fang, Daizong Liu, Jianjun Li, Kun He, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Trajectory Matching Policy Optimization (TMPO) for diffusion model alignment that replaces scalar reward maximization with trajectory-level reward distribution matching to prevent mode collapse and reward hacking.

entry.title: Test-Time Personalization: A Diagnostic Framework and Probabilistic Fix for Scaling Failures

author.name: Linhai Zhang, Yulan He

entry.summary: Studies Test-Time Personalization by scaling inference-time computation via Best-of-N selection. Proves oracle selection grows logarithmically and diagnoses why standard reward models fail through a unified scaling law decomposition.

entry.title: An Execution-Verified Multi-Language Benchmark for Code Semantic Reasoning

author.name: Yikun Li, Jinfeng Jiang, Ting Zhang, Chengran Yang, Chenxing Zhong, Yin Yide, Leow Wen Bin, Eng Lieh Ouh, Lwin Khin Shar, David Lo

entry.summary: Introduces TraceEval, the first execution-verified multi-language benchmark for code semantic reasoning - recovering runtime call structures from source code. Unlike prior benchmarks, every ground truth is validated by actual execution.

entry.title: LoopUS: Recasting Pretrained LLMs into Looped Latent Refinement Models

author.name: Taekhyun Park, Yongjae Lee, Dohee Kim, Hyerim Bae

entry.summary: Introduces LoopUS, converting pretrained LLMs into looped architectures with encoder, looped reasoning block, and decoder for iterative refinement. Avoids training from scratch while enabling test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: Portable Agent Memory: A Protocol for Cryptographically-Verified Memory Transfer Across Heterogeneous AI Agents

author.name: Santhosh Kumar Ravindran

entry.summary: Proposes an open protocol for transferring persistent memory state across heterogeneous AI agents using Merkle-DAG provenance graphs, capability-based access control, and injection-resistant rehydration. Addresses vendor lock-in of agent memory.

entry.title: CATS: Cascaded Adaptive Tree Speculation for Memory-Limited LLM Inference Acceleration

author.name: Yuning Han, Yangchenchen Jin, Dylan Zhao, Jingwei Sun

entry.summary: CATS proposes cascaded adaptive tree speculation for speculative decoding on memory-constrained devices. Addresses the assumption that both target and draft models fit in memory simultaneously.

entry.title: Exploring Token-Space Manipulation in Latent Audio Tokenizers

author.name: Francesco Paissan, Luca Della Libera, Mirco Ravanelli, Cem Subakan

entry.summary: LATTE proposes learnable latent tokens for audio codecs that aggregate global information across utterances, creating a compact non-temporally-aligned bottleneck enabling simple token-space manipulation for speech editing.

entry.title: A Theory of Time-Sensitive Language Generation: Sparse Hallucination Beats Mode Collapse

author.name: Atul Ganju, Travis McVoy, Shaddin Dughmi, Shang-Hua Teng

entry.summary: Provides a theory of time-sensitive language generation where higher-ranked strings must be generated earlier. Shows sparse hallucination beats mode collapse under timeliness constraints for eventually consistent generators.

entry.title: Epistemic Uncertainty for Test-Time Discovery

author.name: Kainat Riaz, Muhammad Ahmed Mohsin, Ahsan Bilal, Muhammad Umer, Ayesha Mohsin, Aqib Riaz, Ali Subhan, John M. Cioffi

entry.summary: UG-TTT uses ensemble of low-rank adapters over frozen base models to measure epistemic uncertainty via per-token disagreement. Targets scientific discovery by distinguishing unexplored regions from difficult problems.

entry.title: Options, Not Clicks: Lattice Refinement for Consent-Driven MCP Authorization

author.name: Ying Li, Yanju Chen, Peiran Wang, Issac Khabra, Faysal Hossain Shezan, Yu Feng, Yuan Tian

entry.summary: Conleash provides consent-driven MCP authorization using a risk lattice to auto-permit safe tool calls while escalating risky ones. Converts user decisions into reusable rules to reduce consent fatigue.

entry.title: Offline Policy Evaluation for Manipulation Policies via Discounted Liveness Formulation

author.name: Hao Wang, Joshua Bowden, Colton Crosby, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: Proposes an offline policy evaluation framework for robotic manipulation using a liveness-based Bellman operator. Addresses challenges of sparse rewards, non-monotonic task progression, and finite-length evaluation rollouts.

entry.title: Keep What Audio Cannot Say: Context-Preserving Token Pruning for Omni-LLMs

author.name: Chaeyoung Jung, Kyeongha Rho, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: Proposes ContextGuard for omnimodal LLMs that preserves broad audio-visual context while removing cross-modal redundancy during token pruning, rather than just selecting query-relevant tokens.

entry.title: Reviving In-domain Fine-tuning Methods for Source-Free Cross-domain Few-shot Learning

author.name: Yaze Zhao, Yicong Liu, Yixiong Zou, Yuhua Li, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: Investigates why adapter-based methods (LoRA) outperform prompt-based methods (MaPLe) for cross-domain few-shot learning with CLIP, finding LoRA rectifies collapsed CLS token attention.

entry.title: Self-organized MT Direction Maps Emerge from Spatiotemporal Contrastive Optimization

author.name: Zhaotian Gu, Molan Li, Jie Su, Chang Liu, Tianyi Qian, Dahui Wang

entry.summary: Uses a spatiotemporal TDANN trained via MoCo on naturalistic videos to show that MT direction-selective maps emerge from the same universal organizational principles as ventral stream topography.

entry.title: Very Efficient Listwise Multimodal Reranking for Long Documents

author.name: Yiqun Sun, Pengfei Wei, Lawrence B. Hsieh

entry.summary: Proposes ZipRerank for efficient listwise multimodal reranking that reduces input length via query-image early interaction and eliminates autoregressive decoding for single-pass scoring.

entry.title: Beyond Point-wise Neural Collapse: A Topology-Aware Hierarchical Classifier for Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Huiyu Yi, Zhiming Xu, Dunwei Tu, Zhicheng Wang, Baile Xu, Furao Shen

entry.summary: Proposes HC-SOINN, a hierarchical classifier that captures manifold topology for class-incremental learning, addressing the failure of Neural Collapse assumptions when classes form complex manifolds.

entry.title: DriftXpress: Faster Drifting Models via Projected RKHS Fields

author.name: Ali Falahati, Elliot Creager, Gautam Kamath, Shubhankar Mohapatra

entry.summary: Introduces DriftXpress, which accelerates drifting models (one-step generative models) by approximating the drifting kernel in a low-rank RKHS feature space, maintaining quality while reducing training computation.

entry.title: Discrete Flow Matching for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Fairoz Nower Khan, Nabuat Zaman Nahim, Peizhong Ju

entry.summary: Introduces DRIFT, an online fine-tuning method for discrete action spaces using continuous-time Markov chain policies with advantage-weighted discrete flow matching and path-space regularization.

entry.title: OmniNFT: Modality-wise Omni Diffusion Reinforcement for Joint Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Guohui Zhang, XiaoXiao Ma, Jie Huang, Hang Xu, Hu Yu, Siming Fu, Yuming Li, Zeyue Xue, Lin Song, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Feng Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes OmniNFT for joint audio-video generation using RL, addressing multi-objective advantage inconsistency, multi-modal gradient imbalance, and uniform credit assignment issues in diffusion-based multimodal generation.

entry.title: MuonQ: Enhancing Low-Bit Muon Quantization via Directional Fidelity Optimization

author.name: Yupeng Su, Ruijie Zhang, Ziyue Liu, Yequan Zhao, Zheng Zhang

entry.summary: MuonQ addresses quantization sensitivity in Muon optimizer training by introducing directional fidelity optimization, including pre-quantization normalization and error correction for low-bit training.

entry.title: FERMI: Exploiting Relations for Membership Inference Against Tabular Diffusion Models

author.name: Abtin Mahyar, Masoumeh Shafieinejad, Yuhan Liu, Xi He

entry.summary: FERMI introduces membership inference attacks against tabular diffusion models that exploit multi-relational structure (parent tables), addressing privacy risks in realistic multi-table data synthesis scenarios.

entry.title: Augmented Lagrangian Method for Last-Iterate Convergence for Constrained MDPs

author.name: Michael Lu, Max Qiushi Lin, Mo Chen, Sharan Vaswani

entry.summary: Proposes augmented Lagrangian method with provable last-iterate convergence for constrained MDPs, addressing the practical mismatch between theory (mixture policies) and deployment (single policy).

entry.title: Block-R1: Rethinking the Role of Block Size in Multi-domain Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Large Language Models

author.name: Yan Jiang, Ruihong Qiu, Zi Huang

entry.summary: Studies block size as a design factor in RL post-training for diffusion large language models, identifying domain conflicts in multi-domain settings and proposing dynamic block size scheduling.

entry.title: Information theoretic underpinning of self-supervised learning by clustering

author.name: Josef Kittler, Sara Atito, Muhammad Awais

entry.summary: Provides information-theoretic foundations for self-supervised learning by clustering, formulating SSL as KL divergence optimization and showing that mode collapse prevention via teacher distribution constraints leads to known batch centering techniques.

entry.title: Lower bounds for one-layer transformers that compute parity

author.name: Daniel Hsu

entry.summary: Proves that one-layer self-attention with rational function post-processing cannot compute parity unless heads × degree grows linearly with input length. Extends the lower bound to ReLU networks via rational approximation.

entry.title: In-context learning to predict critical transitions in dynamical systems

author.name: Yunus Sevinchan, Juan Nathaniel, Kai Ueltzh\"offer, Carla Roesch, Tobias Weber, Vaios Laschos, Hang Fan, Gregor Ramien, Johannes Haux, Pierre Gentine, Benjamin Herdeanu

entry.summary: Introduces TipPFN, an in-context learning framework using prior-data fitted networks to predict critical transitions (tipping points) in dynamical systems. Trained on a novel synthetic data generator and demonstrates prediction of system proximity to critical transitions.

entry.title: Uniform Scaling Limits in AdamW-Trained Transformers

author.name: William Gibson, Christoph Reisinger

entry.summary: Studies the large-depth limit of AdamW-trained transformers by modeling hidden-state dynamics as interacting particle systems. Proves L2 convergence to forward-backward ODE system at rate O(L^{-1} + L^{-1/3}H^{-1/2}), connecting to McKean-Vlasov ODEs.

entry.title: Constrained Stochastic Spectral Preconditioning Converges for Nonconvex Objectives
